refuted.field: next_deadline (sub-claim: "That cycle is closed and its grants have started")
refuted.why: The first half is calendar-true (Jan 27 / May 19 / Sep 1 2026 have all passed as of 2026-09-18) but the second half is an inference with no funder support. AACR publishes no grantee list for this mechanism: the funded-research Career Development Awards index at aacr.org/professionals/research-funding/funded-research/career-development-awards/ names 16 CDA programmes and this is NOT one of them (the only similarly-named entry is the separate "Breast Cancer Research Foundation - AACR Career Development Awards to Foster Diversity and Inclusion"). So nothing on aacr.org confirms that 2026 awards were made or that any grant term began on September 1, 2026. State it as "the 2026 cycle's dates have all passed; AACR has published no grantee list for this mechanism", not as "its grants have started".

Over-precise. AACR gives only months, not dates, for both decision points ("APPLICANTS NOTIFIED OF DECISION STATUS OF LETTER OF INTENT / March 2026"; "NOTIFICATION OF AWARD / July 2026"), so the intervals are ranges, not the single point estimates given. Jan 27 -> March is 5-9 weeks, not "~5 weeks"; May 19 -> July is 6-10.5 weeks, not "~6-7 weeks". The two month-anchored figures that ARE precise (LOI -> Sep 1 funds = ~7.1 months; full application -> funds = 3.5 months) are correct because September 1 is a stated calendar date.

corrections.corrected_value: LOI (Jan 27, 2026) -> invitation decision: stated only as "March 2026", i.e. 5-9 weeks. Full application -> funds: 3.5 months. Start date is a fixed calendar date and eligibility is tested at it: "At the start of the grant term on September 1, 2026, applicants must...". Acceptance obligation confirmed verbatim: "Grant recipients must attend the Annual Grantee Recognition Event during the AACR Annual Meeting to formally accept their grant. Grant funds may be used to support the grantee's registration and travel to this event."

corrections.corrected_value: Claim is verbatim-correct, but incomplete in a way that matters. (1) The R01/DP2/DP5/MIRA exclusion appears ONLY in the PDF guidelines - the web programme page's own "Eligibility Criteria" section does not contain it, so a page-only reader never sees the bar. Full verbatim: "Investigators who are currently, or have been, a Principal Investigator on a substantial independent research award (e.g., an NIH R01 award, DP2 award, DP5 award, MIRA award, or the equivalent) are not eligible. For the purpose of this grant, a substantial independent research award is defined as a grant that offers at least $250,000 (direct) per year for more than three years and must have undergone a peer-review process by active researchers and/or physician-scientists. Qualified investigators are invited to apply for AACR grants for independent investigators." (2) Four further disqualifiers the claim omits, each capable of sinking an application: "Applicants receiving any Investigator-Initiated Study Program (IISP) funds from Merck or are working on a research project that is funded by IISP funds from Merck will not be considered for this grant"; "Scientific investigators or health professionals who are funded by the tobacco industry for any research project are not eligible for any AACR grant"; "Employees or subcontractors of a U.S. government entity or for-profit private industry are not eligible"; and "Current AACR grantees may apply only if their current grant ends before the start of the grant term... (i.e., September 1, 2026)", with final progress reports approved before that date. Postdocs/clinical fellows and Scientific Review Committee members are also barred. (3) There IS a relief valve the claim omits: "An exception to the 6-year window may be granted for parental leave or other well-justified leave from research for pressing personal or family situations of generally less than 12 months' duration" - contact grants@aacr.org before applying.
corrections.source: 2026 Program Guidelines PDF, pages 4-5 and 7 (pdftotext), cross-checked against the eligibility section rendered on the programme page

corrections.corrected_value: All quoted elements confirmed verbatim: LOI Narrative "Limited to two pages, including figures and tables. The References section does not count against this page limit", four mandatory subheadings in order "(A) Specific Aims; (B) Rationale, Preliminary Data, Methodology, and Approach; (C) Statistical Analysis Plan; and (D) Significance and Statement of Relevance"; References "Limited to two pages" in Uniform Requirements style (first six authors then "et al"); "When a template is provided, the template MUST be used"; "Applicants are required to use all templates provided"; "Only PDF attachments are permitted for this Letter of Intent submission"; ProposalCentral via "Filter by Grant Maker" -> "American Association for Cancer Research". Add the formatting rules the claim omits, which carry a hard penalty: "Failure to observe these guidelines will result in the return of the Letter of Intent without review" - 12-point Times New Roman (no smaller than 9-point in figures/legends/tables), single-spaced, margins "no less than 0.75 inches on each side", consecutive page numbering. Also: project title limited to 100 characters; Lay Abstract and Scientific Abstract each limited to 3,000 characters including spaces; LOI package = LOI + Applicant's Biographical Sketch + Applicant Checklist (signed) + Signature Page; the nominator/reference letter (department chair, division head or dean, plus an AACR-member endorser if the nominator is not a member) is required only at the INVITED FULL APPLICATION stage, not at LOI.

Confirmed: a full-text search of the 15-page PDF for resubmit / reapply / unsuccessful / not selected / declined returns zero hits - no bar and no encouragement. One framing correction: the sentence the claim cites as what IS stated - "The Committee will consider each year's applicants independently, without regard to the topics covered in previously funded proposals or to the institutions of the previous grantees" - is about topic and institution diversity across funded proposals, NOT about a prior applicant's right to reapply; do not present it as a resubmission policy. The genuine per-cycle limit is separate: "Investigators may submit only one application for the AACR Career Development Awards to Foster Diversity and Inclusion but may concurrently apply for other AACR grants. However, applicants are expected to accept the first grant they are awarded. Individuals may accept and hold only one AACR grant at a time." Correct answer for the field: not addressed by the funder.

refuted.why: Two factual errors about the surrounding cycle. (1) The claim says ACLS Fellowships is the earliest date and that the 'next cluster' is Oct 28. Refuted: the funder's own deadlines page lists 'The Arnold L. and Lois S. Graves Awards in the Humanities - October 16, 2026, 9:00 PM ET' between Sept 17 and Oct 28. The claim omits it entirely. (2) The claim's '5:00 PM ET' is presented as the ACLS house rule; Graves runs on 9:00 PM ET (nomination Oct 16, 9:00 PM EDT; nominee application Dec 11, 9:00 PM EDT), so the hour is not universal across the cycle. (3) 'The whole ACLS humanities cycle runs Sept-Nov' is refuted: the published 2026-27 deadlines run from Sept 17, 2026 to April 2, 2027 (Nov 20, Jan 13, Feb 1, Mar 10, Apr 2). The annual-rhythm narrative for ACLS Fellowships itself (July open -> Aug/Sept sessions -> mid-Sept deadline -> April notification -> July 1 start) is confirmed; only the cycle-context framing is wrong.

'Nothing carries over... you rebuild from zero each time' is refuted by the fuller FAQ sentence, of which the claim quotes only the second half. Verbatim: 'You may revise the content of your previous application, but you will need to start over with a new online application for the current competition year. You cannot reactivate or edit a previous application in our online system.' Content DOES carry over - the applicant reuses and revises their own prose; only the system record cannot be reactivated. The claim converts a data-entry chore into a rewrite-from-scratch warning, which would wrongly discourage a reapplicant. The 'no stated cap on number of applications' half is confirmed (FAQ and competition page are both silent), and is corroborated by the fellows list, where the same scholars appear in multiple award years.

Sound on every funder-stated anchor, but overstates the Project Development Grant and carries one quote I could not locate. The claim says reaching the final round 'puts you automatically in scope' and quotes 'those who make it to the second round of peer review'. That phrasing does not appear on the competition page or the FAQ as fetched. The funder's actual wording is discretionary, not automatic: 'Applicants from these institutions who are not selected for fellowships, but present particularly promising proposals, MAY be awarded a grant of $5,000' and 'Recipients will be selected within the normal review process from among applicants who advanced to the final stage', offered to 'especially promising applicants from teaching-intensive institutions'. Separately, the stage timings ('~1-4 months', '~4-6 months') are the agent's inference; ACLS states no interim milestones. Confirmed verbatim: three disciplinary scholars at stage one; multidisciplinary final panel; 'Notification of results will be sent via email by April 2027'; reviewer comments 'by August 2027'; award term 'must begin between July 1, 2027, and July 1, 2028, and must be completed by December 31, 2028'; 'At least six months of the award term must be completed consecutively.'

The headline deviation is correct and verbatim ('This program will not accept writing samples. This program will not accept reference letters.'), but the field is materially incomplete on required documents - the point the review asked me to press hardest on. It names the two deleted items and, in what I was given, never enumerates the seven that remain. A reader would infer a light application; it is not. The 'no institutional sign-off / your research office is not in the path' assertion is plausible for an individual fellowship but is NOT funder-stated: no sentence about institutional approval, sponsoring organization or research-office sign-off appears on the competition page. Mark it inferred, not sourced.

Both quoted sentences are accurate verbatim, and the reading of 'accepted, not applied for' is right. But the field is incomplete in the direction that causes real harm: it omits the concurrent-funding cap, which is the live constraint for almost everyone who wins this. The competition page states that an ACLS Fellowship 'may be held concurrently with other fellowships and grants and institutional support (such as sabbatical pay) within limits pre-set by ACLS each competition year', and then sets those limits numerically. A person stacking this on sabbatical pay needs that arithmetic before they plan a year; the claim as written implies the only conflict rules are the two prohibitions. Also note the FAQ's softening is real and worth keeping: 'not more than one ACLS or ACLS-joint award may NORMALLY be accepted in any one competition year.'

corrections.corrected_value: All through ACLS OFA (https://ofa.acls.org). THE DEVIATION IS REAL AND CONFIRMED VERBATIM: 'This program will not accept writing samples. This program will not accept reference letters.' FAQ 2026-27: 'No. In the 2026-27 competition year, this program will not require or accept letters of recommendation as part of the fellowship application package.' But the application is not short. The competition page's requirements list, in full: completed application form; proposal, 'no more than three pages, single-spaced, in Arial or Helvetica 11-point font, inclusive of any footnotes or endnotes'; up to 2 additional pages of images or supporting materials (optional); work plan, max 1 page; bibliography, max 2 pages; publication list, max 2 pages; personal statement, max 1 page. So: six required documents, nine pages of prose plus two optional image pages, and the whole thing is written by you alone with no referee to chase. PAGE LIMIT CLAIM CONFIRMED AND SHARPENED - the 3-page proposal cap is real, and the font/spacing rule is part of it, footnotes included in the count. 'No institutional sign-off' is INFERRED, not funder-stated: ACLS says nothing either way about research-office approval on this page. Treat as probable (the award is individual and paid to the scholar) but unsourced.

WHAT EXCLUDES YOU (verbatim, both confirmed): 'No more than one ACLS or ACLS-joint award may be accepted in any one competition year' - the verb is ACCEPTED, not applied for, so you may hold multiple applications in flight. FAQ softens it further: 'not more than one ACLS or ACLS-joint award may normally be accepted in any one competition year.' And: 'You may not apply for the support of activities that ACLS has already funded with a previous award' - the bar is on the ACTIVITY, not the person; a new project from a former ACLS awardee is not caught, and the funder's own fellows list shows repeat awardees across years. ADD, MISSING FROM THE ORIGINAL AND PRACTICALLY DECISIVE - stacking is allowed but capped: 'An ACLS Fellowship may be held concurrently with other fellowships and grants and institutional support (such as sabbatical pay) within limits pre-set by ACLS each competition year.' The limits: for tenure-track scholars, 'the combination of stipend and sabbatical salary may not exceed the amount of your full academic year salary'; for non-tenure-track scholars, 'combined sources of income may not exceed 150% of the ACLS award.' Maximum award $60,000 for twelve months, $30,000 minimum for a six-month term. NO waiting period after a prior ACLS award is stated anywhere.

Allowed, no stated cap, and unmarked - but the reapplication is a re-entry, not a rewrite. Verbatim FAQ, full sentence: 'You may revise the content of your previous application, but you will need to start over with a new online application for the current competition year. You cannot reactivate or edit a previous application in our online system.' So your prose carries forward; the OFA record does not. Budget a day of re-entry, not a season of rewriting. No limit on number of attempts appears on the competition page or in the FAQ, and the fellows list (2004-2026) shows individual scholars appearing in more than one award year. Do not import the Mellon/ACLS DIF once-only rule here - that is a different mechanism and I did not verify its rule in this pass.

Keep the funder-stated spine, downgrade the PDG line. CONFIRMED VERBATIM: stage one, 'three established scholars in your discipline (and/or regional area of study) will judge your proposal'; stage two, 'a panel of scholars whose collective expertise covers a range of disciplines in the humanities and humanities-related interpretive social sciences'; 'Notification of results will be sent via email by April 2027'; 'you should expect to receive reviewer comments by August 2027'; 'The award term must begin between July 1, 2027, and July 1, 2028, and must be completed by December 31, 2028'; 'At least six months of the award term must be completed consecutively.' So: submission to notification about 6.5 months, to earliest start about 9.5 months, to feedback about 11 months - all sound. CORRECTED: the $5,000 Project Development Grant is discretionary, not automatic. Funder's wording: applicants from teaching-intensive institutions 'who are not selected for fellowships, but present particularly promising proposals, may be awarded a grant of $5,000', and 'Recipients will be selected within the normal review process from among applicants who advanced to the final stage.' It does not require a separate application, which is the part the original got right. The phrase 'those who make it to the second round of peer review' is NOT on the competition page or the FAQ as fetched - do not quote it. The intermediate stage timings ('~1-4 months', '~4-6 months') are inference; ACLS publishes no interim milestones.

refuted.why: PARTIAL REFUTATION, and it is the actionable half. The date is right: both https://www.acls.org/competitions/acls-hbcu-faculty-fellowships/ ("Wednesday, November 11, 2026, 5 PM ET") and https://www.acls.org/competitions-and-deadlines/ ("ACLS HBCU Faculty Fellowships - November 11, 2026, 5:00 PM ET"; "ACLS HBCU Faculty Grants - November 11, 2026, 5:00 PM ET") agree. What is FALSE is the claim's own framing: "TWO EARLIER DATES ... and both are already past for the 2026-27 cycle ... the five applicant office hours, the last of which was Monday, November 2, 2026." Today is 2026-09-18. November 2, 2026 has not happened. Neither has October 13, 2026. Only three of the five sessions (Jul 30, Aug 21, Sep 16) are past. ACLS's own webinars page corroborates this by listing exactly the three sessions that were still live at fetch time (Sep 16, Oct 13, Nov 2). The claim tells a reader in September 2026 that every chance to talk to program staff is gone and that they should look to 2027-28, when in fact two office hours remain and the deadline is seven weeks out. That is the exact failure mode this check exists to catch, inverted: not a stale date sold as current, but a current date sold as stale.

The mechanism-specific facts are confirmed, but the headline contrast is fabricated. Claim: "requires NO REFERENCE LETTERS AT ALL (the flagship expects them)". The flagship page (https://www.acls.org/competitions/acls-fellowships/) states the opposite in its own words: "This program will not accept reference letters." Two real deviations from the ACLS flagship, not three. The traps are spacing/length (5pp double vs 3pp single) and the budget (required here, absent there). The flagship additionally wants a publications list and allows optional supporting materials; neither appears here.

Nov 11, 2026, 5:00 PM ET - submission. corrections.corrected_value: Nominator character limits: the funder CONTRADICTS ITSELF and the corpus should carry both readings. The how-to-nominate prose says the nominator must 'explain why the program qualifies as "computational or data science," identify the reasons why the candidate is appropriate for a fellowship "to promote diversity in computing" (limited to 300 characters each)' -- i.e. 300 for BOTH fields. The live nomination form, which is the binding artifact, caps them differently: 'Disciplinary Qualification (Maximum 300 characters)' but 'Membership in Underrepresented Group (Maximum 200 characters)', with helper text '(limited to 200 characters)'. The claim's 200 figure is CORRECT and matches the enforced form; the 300-each prose on the funder's own page is the stale text. Record 200 with a note that the prose page disagrees, so a future verifier does not 'correct' it back to 300.

NEW drift hazard not in the claims, same shape as the one above: the candidate's motivation statement limit also disagrees between prose and form. how-to-nominate says the candidate 'will be asked to indicate her/his motivation for pursuing the degree (limited to 500 characters)'. The live candidate form says 'Motivation & Goals (Maximum 1000 characters)' and frames it more broadly: 'What is your primary reason for pursuing a graduate degree in data science and/or computational science and what do you hope to accomplish?' A student who drafts to 500 characters is writing half the allowed statement. The form's 1000 is the operative limit. The candidate CV upload is separately specified on the form and must include: all degrees earned to date, a bibliographic listing of all publications authored, leadership and service activities, and any awards or honors. Endorsement statement limit (1000 characters) is consistent across prose and form.

refuted.why: The verbatim quote is real (FY26 NOFO Part VI.A: 'The date specified by the NIFA awarding official as the effective date of the grant must be no later than September 30 of the Federal fiscal year in which the project is approved for support and funds are appropriated for such purpose, unless otherwise permitted by law.'), but two glosses on it fail. (1) 'roughly 5 months from deadline to award' is the verifier-agent's own arithmetic, not a funder statement — the NOFO nowhere states a review-to-award duration, and the clause is a CEILING ('no later than') carrying an escape hatch ('unless otherwise permitted by law'). Presenting a derived ceiling as an expected turnaround is exactly the drift this corpus exists to prevent. (2) The sub-claim that 'the FY23/FY24 early-September deadlines compressed this much further' is wrong on the face of the clause: the deadline is Sept 30 of the fiscal year IN WHICH THE PROJECT IS APPROVED, not the FY in which the application was due. A Sept 5 2024 deadline cannot mean a 25-day review; it means approval falls in the following fiscal year, giving up to ~13 months. The clause constrains the award's effective date within its own approval year, and says nothing about elapsed time from any deadline. Everything else in this field verified verbatim: the two-stage review ('First, we screen each application to ensure that it meets the administrative requirements...'; 'Second, a scientific peer-review process will be used...'), the practitioner-inclusive panel factor, the negotiation clause, reviews returned to the PD, the FAS-program-area review routing, and the 30-day Authorized-Representative warning.

The narrow legal point is CORRECT and I verified it independently: 7 CFR 3430.303 imposes no prior-federal-award bar on pre/postdoctoral fellowship applicants. The prior-award bar in that same section belongs to NEW INVESTIGATOR awards ('must have less than 5 years of postgraduate, career-track experience', cannot have received competitively awarded Federal funds, excepting 'pre- or postdoctoral awards or NRI/AFRI Seed Grants') — a different mechanism. (Verified via GovInfo CFR XML; eCFR 302-redirects non-browser clients to unblock.federalregister.gov, so the search-index route was not usable and GovInfo was.) But the FIELD AS WRITTEN is refuted because its framing — 'WHAT DISQUALIFIES YOU — remarkably little' — omits the single largest disqualifier, which is printed in the funder's own Table 8: 'The postdoctoral PD must be a citizen, national, or permanent resident of the United States.' A postdoc reading this field would conclude they are eligible when a large share of the US postdoc population is not. It also omits that the degree-window evidence is due AT the deadline, not later: 'Documentation from the graduate advisor, graduate committee, or the institution must be provided by the application deadline.' An eligibility field that is right about the obscure bar and silent on the obvious one fails the utility test.

A returned-without-review trap the claims half-captured. refuted.why: The stated outer bound for the award start, "the outer bound is ~end of April 2027", is wrong. The two binding rules are the RFA's "awards will begin the period of performance within three months of the award notification" and the FAQ's "You choose your own start date within 3 months of the award notification, and it must begin on the first of the month (for example, it cannot start on January 17)." With notification by 30/31 Jan 2027, the only first-of-month dates inside the three-month window are 1 Feb, 1 Mar and 1 Apr 2027. 1 May 2027 falls outside it. The last permissible start is 1 April 2027, not end of April. The "earliest realistic start is 1 Feb 2027" half is correct, though the FAQ adds a condition the claim omits: "For projects requiring ethical approvals ... a copy of the approval must be submitted and accepted before the award can start" - so 1 Feb is only reachable by an applicant with no human/animal/rDNA protocol, or with approval already in hand.

"the conflict rules are scoped almost entirely to other Alzheimer's Association awards" is overstated, in two ways. (1) Retaining NIH money during the fellowship is conditional, not a clean carve-out. FAQ: "I received an NIH (K and/or R) award or other funding during my fellowship. Can I keep my fellowship? ... It depends on your fellowship's mandatory effort requirement and your institution's policies." And for non-NIH funders: "In most cases, yes - provided there is no scientific or funding overlap ... if there are overlapping aims, we will need updated aims for review." The RFA also imposes an effort floor that interacts with this: "The Principal Investigator must commit to maintaining at least 50% of their full-time effort to research during the funding period." So the honest statement is that NIH funding is not a bar at application and is usually retainable, subject to effort and overlap - not that the rules ignore non-Association funding. (2) The field omits two Association-history bars that belong in a prior-funding field: "Investigators that have previous Alzheimer's Association awards closed as 'Incomplete' are not eligible to apply without exception. This policy will be strictly adhered to," and "Investigators/organizations who are delinquent in required reporting to the Alzheimer's Association are not eligible to apply."

corrections.corrected_value: PAGE LIMIT IS PER-CFP, NOT A FLAT 3 PAGES. The generic ARA Proposal Template (03.19.2025, text extracted from the PDF) says: "Length: Proposals should be a maximum of 3 pages, not including Appendices." But individual CFPs override it. Spring 2026 evidence: AWS Agentic AI CFP states proposals should be "a maximum of 4 pages, not including Appendices"; AI for Information Security CFP states proposals "are encouraged to be a maximum of 3 pages, not including Appendices" (note 'encouraged to be', which is softer than the template's 'should be'); Amazon 2030 CFP states no page figure at all and defers to the template. Correct guidance: treat 3 pages as the default, and read the specific CFP you are answering for an override before writing. Also confirmed verbatim from the template: formatting is "11-point with commonly used legible font (e.g. Calibri, Times New Roman, or Arial); 1-inch margins on all sides", and "All components should be saved as a single PDF and uploaded to submission site." Appendices do not count toward the limit: Appendix A (references) "Limit two pages"; Appendix B one-page CV of PI ("only to include the 5-6 most relevant papers"), one-page Co-PI CV optional; Appendix C (see prior_funding_conflicts). Body sections in the template: Project Title, PI/Co-PI, Cash funding needed, AWS Promotional Credits needed, Amazon contact (optional), Abstract, Keywords, Introduction, Methods, Expected results ("include milestones with timeline estimates"), Funds needed.

"NOT through the university sponsored-programs office, and no institutional sign-off, cost-share, or authorised-organisational-representative approval is required at application" is an INFERENCE, not a funder statement. No page on amazon.science says institutional sign-off is not required. What the funder actually says, and all that can be sourced: the PI is the applicant and eligibility attaches to the person ("full-time faculty member at an accredited academic institution or a permanent researcher" at a non-profit); the cash is "a one-time unrestricted gift to your Principal Investigator's academic institution or organization"; the template instructs the applicant to upload a single PDF to the submission site. Safe phrasing for an ECR: the application itself is a PI-level upload with no published requirement for an institutional signature, but check your own institution's internal rules on industry gifts before submitting, because the gift lands on the institution.

The headline is right (no prior-funding exclusion) but the field is INCOMPLETE in two ways that change what an applicant must do. (1) PRIOR AMAZON MONEY TRIGGERS A MANDATORY DISCLOSURE DOCUMENT. Template, verbatim: "If you have been funded directly or indirectly by Amazon in the last three years, please include Appendix C." Appendix C is "Previously Funded Project Summary (does not count toward page limit) If you or someone on your project team has received cash funding or AWS Promotional Credits directly or indirectly from Amazon within the past 3 years, please answer the questions below. (Include funding from Amazon through your institution or from the NSF-Amazon Fairness in AI funding grant.)" It asks: project title; funding amount and time; funding source; who the funding was for; how much AWS credit is left; and "a brief summary of the results, papers, and open-source software enabled". Note the trap: this reaches ANYONE on the project team, and explicitly counts the NSF-Amazon Fairness in AI grant — i.e. a federal co-funded award counts as Amazon money for disclosure purposes. (2) THERE ARE REAL ELIGIBILITY BARS, just not funding-based ones. Program rules: PI must be "either a full-time faculty member at an accredited academic institution or a permanent researcher" at a non-profit, at least 18; must "not [be] a paid employee of a government entity (other than an accredited academic institution)" — this excludes national-lab and agency staff scientists, which is the most likely surprise for a US postdoc; must not have worked for Amazon in the past 12 months; must not be immediate family of ineligible personnel; and each PI may "submit only one proposal to the ARA Program per call for proposal period" — so with 5+ topic CFPs sharing one deadline, you must pick ONE.
corrections.source: https://www.amazon.science/research-awards/program-rules; ARA Proposal Template PDF (03.19.2025), Appendix C

refuted.why: The flat claim "Proposals should be a maximum of 3 pages" is refuted as a program-wide rule. It is the generic template's figure, and individual CFPs override it: the AWS Agentic AI (Spring 2026) CFP sets "a maximum of 4 pages, not including Appendices", while the AI for Information Security (Spring 2026) CFP says proposals "are encouraged to be a maximum of 3 pages" and Amazon 2030 prints no figure. Presenting 3 pages as the rule would mislead an applicant into under-writing a 4-page call. This is exactly the drift-sensitive class flagged in the task.

"No institutional sign-off, cost-share, or AOR approval is required at application" is refuted as a sourced claim — no funder page states this. It is an inference from the fact that the PI uploads the PDF and the award is a gift to the institution. The negative was not published by Amazon and should not be presented as funder-stated.

Two of the cited "verbatim from the CFP index" lines are refuted: the index does not contain a Fall 2024 entry or a Spring 2024 entry. Fetched twice today, it runs Spring 2026 / Fall 2025 / Spring 2025 / Winter 2024 / Fall 2023 / Spring 2023 / Fall 2022 / Spring 2022 / Winter 2022 / Fall 2021 plus a Past CFPs link. The dates attributed to those two phantom cycles duplicate Fall 2023's and Spring 2025's printed closes. The headline claim (no call open as of 2026-09-18) is NOT refuted and verifies on two funder pages.

"Two calls per year since 2024" is refuted on the index's own evidence: 2024 shows only Winter 2024 (closed 6 March) — no spring and no fall 2024 entry exists there. Twice-yearly is supported from 2025 onward. Separately, "opens ~1 October" rests on a single observed cycle (Fall 2025) and "each bundling 5-8 topic-specific CFPs" could not be established anywhere on the funder's pages — not found.

Not refuted on its headline (there is genuinely no prior-funding exclusion), but refuted as complete guidance: it omits a MANDATORY document trigger and real eligibility bars. Amazon funding within 3 years — including via your institution and including the NSF-Amazon Fairness in AI grant, and including funding held by anyone on the project team — requires Appendix C. And the rules do bar paid employees of government entities other than accredited academic institutions, anyone who worked for Amazon in the past 12 months, and anyone submitting a second proposal in the same call period. Telling a reader "nothing makes you ineligible" would send a national-lab researcher into a wasted submission.

Two sub-claims are unsupported by anything fetched: the phrase that decisions go "via email to all applicants", and the FAQ budget figure of "one to two graduate students (or a post-doctoral researcher) for one year". Neither appeared on the FAQ, rules, template, or CFP pages retrieved. Not found — treat as unresolved, not as funder-stated. The ~3-month FAQ statement and the observed 3-5 month range both stand.

refuted.why: The quote attributed to the Purdue packet -- that Apple 'requires each of [the university's] nominees to represent a unique research area' -- does not appear in either publicly reachable Purdue document. I read the full 2-page Call for Applications PDF (purduemegrad.blog/.../Call-for-Applications-Apple-Scholars-in-AI_ML-2026.pdf) via pdftotext and the rendered InfoReady competition detail page (freeformCompetitionDetail/2021796); neither contains that sentence or any one-per-area rule. The constraint itself IS real, but the sourced wording is Harvard's, not Purdue's: 'Harvard University may nominate a total of three nominees, limited to one nominee from these research areas' (careernavigator.gradeducation.hms.harvard.edu, 30 June 2026). Do not publish the Purdue attribution.

Claim says Harvard's internal packet is 'CV, 2-page research statement, 1-page confidential advisor letter, as a single PDF'. Harvard's page separates them: 'Interested applicants should send their materials as a single PDF. The confidential letter of support should be sent separately.' The advisor letter is explicitly NOT in the single PDF, and is confidential (Michigan likewise: 'Recommendation letters are confidential and not shared with the applicant'). An applicant following the claim as written would bundle a letter that is supposed to arrive independently.

The load-bearing half of this claim is unverifiable and internally inconsistent. The screening-question quote -- 'Do you/will you hold another industry-sponsored fellowship beginning Fall 2025? This does not refer to Purdue funding, or funding...' -- appears on neither of Purdue's two publicly reachable pages; it would sit inside the logged-in InfoReady application form, behind Purdue SSO, which I could not reach. Worse, 'beginning Fall 2025' is inconsistent with this cycle's stated award window of Fall 2027 to Summer 2029, so it reads as stale text carried over from an earlier cycle. Publishing an unsourced carve-out is the exact failure mode that tells an eligible person they are fine when they are not. The EXCLUDES half of the claim is confirmed; the PRESERVES half is not.

The three universities do not state it identically. Michigan: 'Nominee must not hold another industry-sponsored full fellowship while they are an Apple Scholar in AI/ML (Fall 2027 to Summer 2029).' UCL: 'Nominees must not hold another industry-sponsored full fellowship while they are an Apple Scholar in AI/ML (Fall/Autumn 2027 to Summer 2029).' Purdue: 'Must not hold another industry-sponsored full fellowship while an Apple Scholar in AI/ML (Fall 2027 to Summer 2029).' Substantively the same rule, three different sentences. Only Michigan's matches the claimed verbatim string.

The quote -- that Apple's criteria are 'taken from the official nomination guide, which is not publically available' -- is not in Purdue's Call for Applications PDF (I read all 2 pages) nor on the rendered InfoReady detail page. It cannot be cited as Purdue's words on the evidence I could reach.

'Three weeks to score and rank nominee applications using a rubric-survey' and 'may not sit on the applicant's dissertation committee' are not on either public Purdue page -- they would be in the Review Panel Commitment Form, which InfoReady lists as a supporting document but serves only behind Purdue SSO. What Purdue does state publicly is narrower: 'Your department is required to commit one faculty reviewer per Apple applicant, to a maximum of three reviewers per department.' Mark the rest not found.

corrections.corrected_value: CONFIRMED and should stay dated. 8 September 2026 is real, current-cycle, and now past. Verified verbatim on three university pages via a rendering browser (all three 403 a plain fetch): Michigan 'Sponsor Submission Deadline: September 8, 2026'; Harvard 'if you are nominated, the full application -- due on September 8 -- requires additional, more extensive materials than the internal submission'; UCL 'their applications will be submitted to Apple by 8th September 2026, at the latest.' Apple's own site publishes no deadline at all -- machinelearning.apple.com/updates/apple-scholars-aiml-2026 says only that 'Scholars are nominated by their universities', program 'open to invited institutions', contact aiml_scholars@apple.com. ADD one date the claim missed: Purdue's own upload to Apple was earlier than Apple's close -- 'before Purdue uploads them to Apple's portal on September 4, 2026' (InfoReady). So the governing date is your institution's, and even the university-to-Apple handoff can precede 8 September. The early-September-2027 figure remains a projection, correctly labelled as such.

CONFIRMED, with one date I could not verify and one to add. Verified verbatim: internal calls posted 30 Jun 2026 (Harvard) and 13 Jul 2026 (Michigan); internal deadlines 21 Jul 2026 noon (Harvard, 'by noon on July 21, 2026'), 28 Jul 2026 23:59 (UCL, 'Deadline to apply: 11:59 PM, Tuesday 28th July 2026'), 31 Jul 2026 23:59 ET (Purdue, both the PDF and InfoReady), 3 Aug 2026 17:00 (Michigan, 'Internal Competition Deadline: August 3, 2026 (by 5PM)'); nominee notification ~21 Aug (Purdue: 'We anticipate notifying all applicants about the outcome of the nominee selection by approximately August 21'); UCL 'contacted in late August/early September'; Apple closes 8 Sep 2026; outcomes to universities by December 2026; cohorts announced 26 Mar 2025 and 21 Apr 2026 (both confirmed on machinelearning.apple.com). Publish only the EXCLUDES rule, and quote Michigan: 'Nominee must not hold another industry-sponsored full fellowship while they are an Apple Scholar in AI/ML (Fall 2027 to Summer 2029).' Three words are load-bearing: industry-sponsored, FULL, and 'while they are'. Drop the Purdue carve-out sentence entirely until it can be sourced. The claim also omits the eligibility gates that actually disqualify more people than the fellowship-conflict rule does, all verbatim and all confirmed: 'Nominee must currently be enrolled full time at the nominating university, and expect to be enrolled through the end of the 2028/2029 academic year'; 'Nominee should be entering their last two to three (2-3) years of study as of Fall 2026'; Purdue adds 'Anticipated graduation date should be approximately between May-August 2029'; Michigan adds 'Students attending universities in the United States who are starting the first year of their PhD at the time of nomination may not be nominated. The program is targeted towards mid-to-late career PhD students with an established research and publication record'; Harvard states it bluntly: 'G1s are not eligible.' Michigan also names the one authority that can settle a borderline case: 'If you are still uncertain about your eligibility please contact the sponsor directly: aiml_scholars@apple.com.'

CONFIRMED in full, from two independent sources. UCL, 'in line with Apple's specifications': up to 2 of Apple's research areas; research proposal title; 'Research Abstract (200 word maximum)'; CV and publication list; research statement '4 page maximum, including citations, in a legible font size) clearly stating the hypothesis and expected contributions to the chosen research area'; '2 letters of recommendation, one from current advisor (1 page maximum per letter)'; 'Link to most recent published work (optional).' Purdue independently states the same '200 words maximum' abstract and '4-page maximum including citations, in a legible font size' statement, '(1 page maximum per letter)', and that only ONE letter is required internally ('Reference Letters Required per Applicant: 1') with the second due after nomination. ADD two operational details the claim omits, both actionable: Apple's file-naming convention, quoted by UCL -- 'Last name, First name - Research Statement', 'Last name, First name - Resume', 'Last name, First name - Letters of recommendation' (both letters combined into a single PDF) -- and the redaction instruction, 'Please remove or redact birth date, any other personally identifiable information, and/or photographs of yourself before submitting', plus 'Nomination materials should not contain confidential or proprietary research.' The page-limit trap the claim identifies is real and confirmed: Harvard's internal statement is a 'two-page maximum, including citations', against Apple's four.

CONFIRMED on the timeline and on the blinding. UCL verbatim: 'Apple will then run their own application evaluation process and nominating universities will hear back regarding the status of their students' applications by December 2026', and on the statement format, 'Personally identifiable information is redacted for phase one reviewers. We recommend not including personally identifiable information in the main body of the research statement in order to maintain research statement clarity for reviewers of the redacted copy.' Award period 'Fall 2027 to Summer 2029' confirmed by Michigan, UCL and Purdue. Public cohort posts 26 Mar 2025 and 21 Apr 2026 confirmed on Apple's own site, so individual notification does precede the public post by months. Strip the unsourced Purdue reviewer mechanics (see refuted).

Replace the unsourceable quote with what is actually reachable. (1) Purdue's InfoReady competition page names its supporting documents -- 'Apple Research Areas', 'Research Statement Guidance', 'Reference Letter Guide', 'Call for Applications', 'Review Panel Commitment Form' -- but only the Call for Applications PDF is publicly downloadable; the guidance documents sit behind Purdue SSO, so a non-Purdue reader cannot obtain them. (2) The best publicly reachable substitute for Apple's closed guide is Harvard's page, which reproduces all 13 Apple research areas WITH Apple's own definitions and full sub-topic lists (e.g. On-Device and Efficient AI, sub-topics 'Model Compression and Efficient Architectures, Hardware-Aware Training and Inference, TinyML and Energy-Efficient AI...'). That is the single most useful public artefact for someone deciding which two areas to rank. (3) Apple's cohort pages name the 20 scholars per year, which is the only public signal of what a winning profile looks like. No funded application text is published anywhere I could reach.

The claim's practical instruction is right and should be kept, and the pages give the named offices to put in it: your graduate school's limited-submission or fellowships office (Michigan: fellowshipLSO@umich.edu, routed through the Office of the Vice President for Research; Purdue: trainee-funding@purdue.edu, which also connects applicants to a Fellowship Writing Coach; Harvard: gsasacademicprograms@fas.harvard.edu for submission, gsas-fwc@fas.harvard.edu for process questions; UCL: docschool@ucl.ac.uk). Note UCL's disclaimer, which sets expectations correctly: 'The fellowship is run externally by Apple and we are unable to answer questions about the fellowship programme itself beyond what's available on this webpage.' The only route to Apple itself is aiml_scholars@apple.com, and only for eligibility. Contact window for the next cycle: May-June, before internal calls post in late June.

Disclosure for the record. No search index was available -- this session's WebSearch budget was exhausted (200/200) before my first call -- so every claim above is checked against a primary page. ucl.ac.uk, micde.umich.edu and careernavigator.gradeducation.hms.harvard.edu each returned HTTP 403 to a plain fetch and were read through a rendering browser at their own URLs. Purdue's PDF was fetched and extracted with pdftotext; Purdue's InfoReady page was rendered (it is a JS app that returns an empty body otherwise). Apple's two cohort pages fetched normally. Purdue's logged-in application form and its supporting documents were not reachable, which is why three quoted passages could not be checked -- that is a tooling limit, not evidence the passages are false.

refuted.why: The sub-claim 'Missing pre-application is one of only THREE grounds for automatic rejection' is false as a family-wide statement. It is true of PCRP EIRA and MRP MASA (both list exactly: Project Narrative missing / Budget missing / Pre-application not submitted), but the FY26 PRP EIRA announcement lists FIVE rejection grounds (pdftotext of HT942526PRPEIRA_GG.pdf, section 9.2.1): 'The Project Narrative is missing. The Budget is missing. The Pre-application was not submitted. Attachment 7: Letter of Eligibility is missing. Attachment 9: Researcher Development Plan is missing from the Funding Level 1 application.' An applicant told there are only three rejection triggers could lose a PRP Funding Level 1 application by omitting Attachment 7 or 9. Everything else in the loi_required field (mandatory LOI, no screening, no invitation, eBRAP log number required in SF424 Block 4a, PCRP one-page LOI, PRP LOI carrying the min-2/max-3 list of recommenders) was confirmed verbatim.

The claim 'Two-step shape, constant across the family: mandatory pre-application (LOI) first, full application 2-3 weeks later' is refuted as a family-wide generalisation. The 2-3 week gap holds only for the three career-stage announcements read (PCRP Aug 12 to Sep 2 = 3 wks; MRP Sep 22 to Oct 14 = 3 wks; PRP Oct 23 to Nov 6 = 2 wks). Across the rest of the open FY26 CDMRP portfolio the gap is routinely ~3 MONTHS: BMFRP Investigator-Initiated and Idea Development Awards, pre-app Aug 5, 2026 / app Nov 4, 2026; TBIPHRP Clinical Trial and Translational Research Awards, pre-app Jul 13, 2026 / app Oct 15, 2026; BCRP Breakthrough Award Levels 3 and 4 and Transformative Breast Cancer Consortium Award, pre-app Jun 12, 2026 / app Sep 30, 2026. The two-step shape itself and the ~6-7 day verification window ARE constant (PCRP 6 days, MRP 6 days, PRP 7 days), as are the 5:00 p.m. ET / 11:59 p.m. ET clock times. Separately, the supporting statement 'no FY26 mechanism named literally Career Development Award was found in any of the six open programmes checked' reached the right answer but its list of six was wrong: cdmrp.health.mil/funding/ names the six programmes with open opportunities as Bone Marrow Failure, Breast Cancer, Melanoma, Parkinson's, Reconstructive Transplant Research and Traumatic Brain Injury and Psychological Health. PCRP (closed) was counted and RTRP was not checked. I checked RTRP: its two FY26 mechanisms are the Concept Award and the Investigator-Initiated Research Award (both pre-app Oct 21, 2026 / app Nov 4, 2026), neither career-stage, so the conclusion stands.

CONFIRMED as stated - the gate is career stage and appointment, not grant history; no prior or current research grant disqualifies. Adding four disqualifiers in RFA section 7 that the delivered field does not list and that can bite an otherwise-eligible senior postdoc: (1) "A PI who has accepted a position as a tenure-track assistant professor at the recruiting institution prior to the time that the Scientific Review Council meets to review the recruitment application is not eligible" - signing the offer early kills the award; (2) "The PI must devote at least 70% effort to research activities. OTHER REQUIRED PIECES, all CDA-specific and all omitted by the prior answer: FUTURE CAREER PLANS STATEMENT, 2 pages max, placed at the end of the Research Plan section, stating career goals and their relevance to T1D research. DEPARTMENT HEAD STATEMENT — institutional assurance of academic commitment, uploaded as a Supporting Document. PI BIOSKETCH (Breakthrough T1D or NIH format accepted). TWO ABSTRACTS, one scientific and one lay; the lay one broken into 6 named categories (General Audience Summary, Technical Abstract, Objective, Background/Rationale, Anticipated Outcome, Relevance to type 1 diabetes), each capped at 600 words. OTHER SUPPORT, current and pending, for the PI. BUDGET: max USD 200,000/year including indirect costs, indirects capped at 10% of subtotal direct costs (excluding equipment), travel capped at USD 2,000/year. OPTIONAL TICK-BOX: consent to share the application with The Leona M. and Harry B. Helmsley Charitable Trust for potential co-funding. SUBMISSION MECHANICS: the PI clicks 'Validate and Submit Proposal to RO' — the Research Officer submits to Breakthrough T1D, so your institutional internal deadline precedes 5:00pm ET on the funder's date. FORMATTING/COMPLETENESS FAILURES ARE FATAL: 'Failure to submit all required application documents online, failure to submit a budget, biosketches, or any other component of the application, or failure to adhere to the guidelines below will result in administrative triage.' TERM NOTE, funder text is self-inconsistent: front matter and the Handbook table say 5 years / 'generally not renewable after 5 years', while Terms of the Award says twice that awards are 'renewable pending satisfactory progress up to a maximum of four years' — most coherent reading is year 1 plus up to 4 annual renewals = 5 years total, each renewal requiring an approved renewal proposal and an annual progress report.

refuted.field: next_deadline — the absolute phrasing "There is NO annual ECP competition deadline"
refuted.why: Over-strong. The date 20 Nov 2027 is correct and I confirmed it three ways (BAA Amendment 4 cover page verbatim "21 November 2022 - 20 November 2027"; Grants.gov fetchOpportunity id 344592 revision 11 — postingDate Nov 21 2022, responseDate Nov 20 2027, archiveDate Dec 20 2027, lastUpdatedDate Aug 11 2026; and ARL's own live BAA page still serving Amendment 4 as current, i.e. no Amendment 5 exists). But ARL HAS run a dated ECP competition against this same BAA as a special notice: the HBCU/MI Early Career Program Special Notice (grants.gov attachment id 332764, posted 1 Nov 2023, referencing W911NF-23-S-0001-0002), which states proposals "must be received no later than 4:00 PM (ET), January 12, 2024" and "An award announcement is expected by March 2024." That notice is expired and no live ECP special notice is currently posted, so the practical answer for a general applicant today is unchanged — but the categorical claim is false, and an HBCU/MI applicant who relies on it will miss a real deadline.

refuted.field: prior_funding_conflicts — "The sole eligibility gate is status and citizenship"
refuted.why: Incomplete in the exact direction the task warns about (telling an eligible person not to apply). The BAA's very next sentence is a carve-out the claim omits entirely: "Faculty at an institution of higher education which does not designate a faculty appointment as 'tenure track' are eligible if that fact is so indicated in the proposal, and the supporting letter from the institute states that the faculty member submitting the proposal will be considered for a permanent appointment." Rendering the gate as tenure-track-only excludes a whole class of eligible applicants (teaching-intensive institutions, research-institute appointments, institutions without tenure systems). Separately, the HBCU/MI ECP variant DOES define the early-career clock by prior funding — "within five years of receiving his or her first competitively awarded federal research funding (as principal investigator), excluding funds secured during graduate school or postdoctoral training/fellowship and funds secured for training, fellowship, education, or career development" — so "this mechanism has essentially no prior-funding exclusion" is right for mainline ECP and wrong for that variant.

corrections.corrected_value: On "why was the dated deadline forbidden": nothing in the house rules forbids showing a real date. The rule forbids INVENTING one and forbids presenting a past cycle's date as the next deadline — "an empty field is a correct answer; an invented deadline is a failure." 20 November 2027 is real, current, and triple-sourced, so it belongs in the interface. What it must not be labelled is "next deadline," because that word makes a postdoc plan backwards from a date that is actually an expiry. result.program_name: Early Career Research Program (ECRP) — U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Science

refuted.why: MISATTRIBUTED QUOTE + a live contradiction between two funder documents. The claim says pre-applications are scored 'by "no less than three federal program managers"'. That phrase is NOT in the FY2026 NOFO (DE-FOA-0003602). The NOFO's own words are: 'Any such review will be concurred in by no less than three SC-affiliated individuals chosen for their topical knowledge and diversity of perspective.' The 'federal program managers' wording exists only in the FY2026 FAQ (A57: 'These reviews will be conducted by no less than three federal program managers chosen for their topical knowledge and diversity of perspective'). So the quote is real but comes from the FAQ, not the NOFO, and the controlling document says something broader (SC-affiliated individuals, not necessarily program managers). Source: https://science.osti.gov/-/media/grants/pdf/foas/2026/DE-FOA-0003602.pdf and https://science.osti.gov/-/media/grants/pdf/foas-resources/2026/Early-Career-FAQ-FY-2026_03_20.pdf

OVERSTATED AS UNIVERSAL. The claim asserts flatly 'IT IS A COMPETITIVE CUT, NOT A HEADCOUNT' and that pre-applications are scored against four criteria. Both funder documents make the competitive scoring CONDITIONAL. NOFO: 'SC may evaluate all or some portion of pre-applications to determine their competitiveness within a scientific topic' and 'Topics with comparatively few pre-applications may not make use of such pre-application reviews. The ratio of encourage/discourage results will differ between topical subjects.' FAQ A57: the four criteria apply 'if a scientific topic receives a large number of pre-applications'. The mandatory, universal test is responsiveness; the comparative cut is discretionary and topic-dependent. Correct statement: every pre-application is screened for responsiveness; in over-subscribed topics it is additionally rank-scored on the four criteria.

UNSUPPORTED SUB-CLAIM: 'a regulatory backstop of 12 months under 10 CFR 605.10'. Not found. Neither the ECRP NOFO nor the Open Call NOFO (DE-FOA-0003600, Amendment 000001) states a 12-month decision backstop. Both cite 10 CFR 605.10 only for (b) the initial/responsiveness review and (d) the merit-review criteria. The Open Call's six-month figure IS confirmed verbatim: 'DOE anticipates making funding decisions within six months. The time interval begins on the date the application is received.' The 12-month figure should be marked not found unless sourced to the eCFR text itself.

corrections.corrected_value: CONFIRMED with one internal DOE discrepancy on the issue date. Verified 2026-09-18 on the funder's own pages: the Open NOFO list shows only DE-FOA-0003657 (closes 19 Oct 2026), DE-FOA-0003612 (closes 17 Dec 2026) and the Open Call DE-FOA-0003600 (closes 30 Sept 2026) — no ECRP NOFO is open, so there is genuinely no FY2027 date to publish. The stale-page trap is also confirmed: science.osti.gov/early-career still displays 'Pre-applications: March 24, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. ET' and 'Full applications: June 2, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. ET' on 2026-09-18, more than three months after that deadline. ISSUE-DATE CORRECTION: the NOFO cover reads 'NOFO Issue Date: March 3, 2026' (confirmed in the PDF), but DOE's own Closed NOFO list dates DE-FOA-0003602 to March 2, 2026. Cite the cover; note the list disagrees by a day. FY2025 (DE-FOA-0003450) confirmed on the Closed list: issued 17 Jan 2025, pre-app 18 Feb 2025 5:00 PM ET, application 22 Apr 2025 11:59 PM ET — so the five-week year-on-year drift is real.

Substance CONFIRMED, but the three-attempt cap needs its carve-outs stated or it will scare off eligible people. NOFO §II.D: 'Only one pre-application on behalf of a PI may be submitted in any given SC ECRP competition. A PI may not submit an application in more than three SC ECRP competitions.' WHAT COUNTS AS AN ATTEMPT — the NOFO itself gives two slightly different definitions, and the carve-outs matter: (a) §II.D: 'Participation in the competition is defined as submission of a full application that completed the review/decision process'; (b) the title-page footnote: 'submission of a full, formal application with two exceptions: applications withdrawn from consideration prior to official declination of the application do not count as a submission, and applications declined without merit review by the DOE SC do not count as a submission. A PI who has participated in three past SC ECRP competitions is not eligible.' (c) FAQ Q67: a DISCOURAGED pre-application does not count toward the three attempts. (d) FAQ Q69: an encouraged pre-application you chose not to follow up does not count. PRIOR AWARD: confirmed permanent — 'PIs who have received awards previously under the SC ECRP are not eligible' (FAQ Q13: 'No.'). CARVE-OUT CONFIRMED AND IMPORTANT: 'PIs of early career awards funded by other agencies or entities are eligible, but the proposed research must have a scope different from that already funded by the other organization' — i.e. an NSF CAREER holder IS eligible (FAQ Q98 allows simultaneous NSF CAREER / DOE ECRP submission, 'but you can only be funded once by the federal government for a given scope'). FAQ Q97: 'The application may not duplicate your currently funded research, regardless of the agency funding it.'

MISSING FROM THE CLAIMS AND MORE DECISIVE THAN ANY DEADLINE — the ten-year PhD clock, which is what actually rules most people in or out. NOFO: 'No more than 10 years can have passed between the year the PI's Ph.D. was awarded and the calendar year at the start of the Federal fiscal year in which this NOFO is released. For the present competition, those who received doctorates on or after January 1, 2015, are eligible.' The 2015 date is FY2026-specific and will move each cycle — treat it as drift-sensitive, never carry it forward. EXTENSIONS: for major life events of three months or longer, 'must be validated by a letter from the university dean, research vice president, laboratory division director, or equivalent official. The letter must be included in the pre-application.' FAQ Q8 confirms no advance ruling ('the letter requesting an eligibility extension will be evaluated as part of the pre-application process') and Q9 confirms an extension does not carry over between years. UNIVERSITY PIs: must be untenured and on the tenure track as of the application due date; FAQ Q14 — tenure granted before the due date makes you ineligible, tenure granted after the due date but before award does not.

CONFIRMED verbatim, no corrections. Page limit: 'The Project Narrative must not exceed a page limit of 15 pages of technical information, including charts, graphs, maps, photographs, and other pictorial presentations' ... 'Merit reviewers will only consider the number of pages specified in the first sentence of this paragraph. This page limit does not apply to the Title Page, Budget Page(s), Budget Justification, biographical material, publications and references, appendices, and an optional table of content.' FAQ Q96 confirms the table of contents is excluded; Q84 confirms the required header block may sit on a separate cover page outside the narrative. NO CO-PIs confirmed and stronger than the claim stated: 'Awards under the Early Career Research Program must be under the sole and indivisible leadership of the PI. Other senior or key personnel ... must commit less time and effort and request less support than the PI ... There can be no co-PIs. Applications including co-PIs may be declined without review.' Pre-application three-page limit confirmed: 'Not including the title page, the pre-application may not exceed three pages ... The body text font must not be smaller than 11 point. Figures and references, if included, must fit within the three-page limit' (FAQ Q65, Q66 confirm). Title page may run to two pages (FAQ Q111: 'Yes'). The no-reviewers list is confirmed as an 'Additional Attachment' in PAMS, excluded from the page limit, and 'rarely empty because the instructions contain mandatory inclusions requirements.' Also confirmed: 'You cannot draft or edit a pre-application in PAMS' and the 'Submit to DOE' privilege requirement (FAQ Q64). DMSP required in Appendix 4 (FAQ Q78), 2-page limit, not counted in the narrative.

CONFIRMED in substance, with a grep trap worth naming. The controlling text is under TYPE OF APPLICATION (FIELD 8): 'A new application is one in which DOE support for the proposed research is being requested for the first time. Only new applications will be considered under this NOFO.' TRAP: the NOFO does contain a heading 'RESUBMISSION OF APPLICATIONS', but it has nothing to do with NIH-style resubmission — it covers withdrawing an application in PAMS and submitting again while the same NOFO is still open: 'After an application is withdrawn, it may be resubmitted, if this NOFO is still open for the submission of applications. Such resubmissions will only count as one submission.' Anyone keyword-searching 'resubmission' will land on this and mis-report it.

CONFIRMED apart from the 12-month backstop. NOFO Section VII.B verbatim: 'It is anticipated that the award selection will be completed by July 2026. It is expected that awards will be made in Fiscal Year 2026.' FAQ Q116 verbatim: 'We suggest a start date of September 1, 2026. Please feel free to indicate any desired date: We can always negotiate a different date after merit review and award selection. The date mentioned in an application is not binding.' Open Call comparison confirmed from DE-FOA-0003600 Amendment 000001: 'DOE anticipates making funding decisions within six months. The time interval begins on the date the application is received.' Review mechanics confirmed verbatim: FAQ Q115 (mail or panel review, each program decides), Q119 (reviewer comments in PAMS at or shortly after recommendation/declination), Q120 (not score-ranked; program policy factors including 'ensuring opportunities to investigators not currently supported by DOE, and increasing participation of institutions historically underrepresented in the SC research portfolio'), Q77 (no Field Work Proposal at application; requested later only from those selected) and Q76 (do not use Searchable FWP). Scale confirmed on the NOFO's Funding Details table: '$145 million total, including $79 million in FY 2026 funding and $66 million in outyear funding', 'Expected number of awards 100', '$875,000 for an Institution of Higher Education', '$2,750,000 for a DOE/NNSA National Laboratory', project period 5 years.

CONFIRMED. Recurrence language confirmed verbatim, FAQ Q117: 'Our intention is to continue this program on an annual basis, subject to availability of funds.' — and the same answer adds the cap: 'a PI may not participate in more than three Office of Science Early Career Research Program competitions over time.' Sixteen-year history confirmed in the NOFO: 'The program has been offered in 16 previous years, FY 2010 - FY 2025.' Late-submission grounds confirmed verbatim: 'DOE has accepted late submissions when applicants have been unable to make timely submissions because of widespread technological disruptions or significant natural disasters. DOE has made accommodations for incapacitating or life-threatening illnesses and for deaths of immediate family members', with unacceptable justifications listed including 'Failure to satisfy prerequisite registrations.' — which directly supports the claim's planning-window point (21 days from NOFO issue to pre-application close in FY2026; registrations must be done beforehand). Late pre-application relief via PAMS help desk confirmed (FAQ Q73). Carry-over confirmed: the DOE Title Page of the full application requires the 'PAMS Pre-application tracking number'; FAQ Q91 confirms 'A slight change in the title is allowed, but the topic may not change.'

CONFIRMED. science.osti.gov/early-career links per-fiscal-year funded-abstract PDFs for FY2010 through FY2025 inclusive (16 separate PDFs), verified present on the live page 2026-09-18. The NOFO itself points there: 'You can learn about the history of the ECRP program at https://science.osti.gov/early-career'. I pulled the current regulation directly from the eCFR versioner API (full title-34 XML, part=662, issue date 2026-09-16) and read 662.21 in full. It contains NO point values anywhere. It lists six unweighted considerations under (b) Quality of proposed project and five under (c) Qualifications of the applicant, and it expressly pushes the weights elsewhere: 662.21(a) verbatim — "The Secretary informs applicants of the maximum possible score for each criterion in the application package or in a notice published in the Federal Register." The point splits the agent quotes are REAL and EXACTLY right, but they live in the FY2025 NIA at 89 FR 86327-86328, which itself says "The selection criteria for this competition are from the regulations for this program in 34 CFR 662.21 and are as follows: (a) Quality of proposed project. (63 points)... (b) Qualifications of the applicant. (37 points)...". This matters for utility, not pedantry: a student sent to the live eCFR for "the published point-weighted rubric" finds criteria with no weights, and the document that actually carried the weights was WITHDRAWN on 9 May 2025 — so as of today the weighted rubric has no in-force authoritative home and can only be read off a withdrawn notice. INCOMPLETE ON TIEBREAKS — "Ties are broken by the Fulbright Foreign Scholarship Board's veteran's-preference policy" states only step one of a four-step chain. If a tie still exists, the average score for selection criterion (a)(1) under ``Quality of proposed project'' (20 points) will be used as the tiebreaker. As a final tiebreaker, should it become necessary, we will use the average score assigned for the ``Qualifications of the applicant'' selection criterion." For an applicant this is actionable — it means criterion (a)(1), the hypotheses/methods statement, is the de facto second-order ranking criterion, which is a concrete drafting instruction the current text loses.

corrections.corrected_value: The point-weighted rubric is NOT in the regulation. 34 CFR 662.21 lists the criteria unweighted and says only: "The Secretary informs applicants of the maximum possible score for each criterion in the application package or in a notice published in the Federal Register." The weights come from the notice. Last published weights (FY2025 NIA, 89 FR 86327-86328 — note this notice was WITHDRAWN 9 May 2025, so treat as historical guidance, not a live rubric): Quality of proposed project, 63 points total — (1) hypotheses/questions + research methods, 20; (2) relationship to literature and theory, originality/importance, 10; (3) preliminary research already done and availability of data in host country, 10; (4) justification for overseas fieldwork + research contacts/affiliations abroad, 10; (5) plans to share results and the dissertation with host-country scholars and officials, 3; (6) guidance and supervision by the dissertation advisor/committee, 10. Qualifications of the applicant, 37 points total — (1) overall strength of graduate academic record, 10; (2) strength in relevant area studies, 10; (3) proficiency in host-country language(s) other than English, 10; (4) steps taken to improve advanced language proficiency for this project, 5; (5) ability to work in a foreign cultural context, per references or prior overseas experience, 2. Reading these together: methods + advisor supervision + literature/originality are 40 of 100 points, and language is 15.

Also add, from 34 CFR 662.20, two selection facts the field omits: 662.20(b) "The Secretary does not consider applications to carry out research in a country in which the United States has no diplomatic representation" — a hard country exclusion that can void a project outright; and 662.20(e)/(f), the Secretary weighs "information on budget, political sensitivity, and feasibility from binational commissions or United States diplomatic missions" before recommending to the FFSB, which "reviews the recommendations and approves recipients."

34 CFR 662.11 in full: "An institution of higher education that participates in this program is responsible for-- (a) Making fellowship application materials available to its students; (b) Accepting and screening applications in accordance with its own technical and academic criteria; and (c) Forwarding screened applications to the Secretary and requesting an institutional grant." Two further campus-gate facts worth adding, both from the FY2025 NIA: the G6 workflow is that doctoral students complete their forms and "submit them to their home IHE project director using G6", i.e. the student never transmits to ED; and if the IHE wants to submit on PAPER instead it must notify ED at least 14 calendar days before the deadline (email received, or mail postmarked, by then) — a second, earlier institutional gate.

Both stated disqualifiers verified verbatim against 89 FR 86325 and 34 CFR 662.22(b), and I could not find a third. Add the CARVE-OUT explicitly, because its absence is what makes eligible people self-reject: the bar is narrow. 662.22(b) prohibits only "more than one graduate fellowship under the Fulbright-Hays Act from appropriations for a given fiscal year", and the NIA operationalises it solely against the Fulbright U.S. Student Program. refuted.why: The quoted rules are all verbatim-correct, but the FRAMING is wrong and it is the drift-sensitive part. The claim says 'almost nothing blocks you at APPLICATION time — the conflicts bite only on activation.' Both halves fail against the AY2027 guidelines. (i) Section 6.3 is a whole-tenure concurrency rule, not an at-activation test: 'HFSP Fellows cannot concurrently hold an HFSP Fellowship and another paid employment position (i.e., a position supported by a salary) or another paid fellowship from another organization' — it binds for the full 36 months, and 'HFSP Fellows must devote themselves entirely to their research project in the host institution and may not engage in any other paid activity without prior agreement by HFSPO.' (ii) Several hard blocks bite at LOI/application time, not activation: 'An HFSP postdoctoral fellowship may only be held once' (Sec 3.1) disqualifies you before you apply; 'each applicant may submit only one Letter of Intent' per year (Sec 3.1); 'any host supervisor can endorse only ONE fellowship application (LOI) per competition year' (Sec 3.6) — a supervisor-side block that can kill your LOI before you write it; the PhD clock is pinned to the Full Proposal date, 'applicants whose doctoral degree was conferred prior to 24 September 2023 are not eligible' (Sec 3.7); and the lead-author publication must already be published/in press/accepted/preprinted-and-submitted AT THE LOI STAGE (Sec 3.8, Table 2). Telling an applicant the conflicts only matter at activation is exactly the error that wastes a cycle.

'Everything is typed into ProposalCentral text boxes — there is NO uploaded proposal document for fellowships' is over-stated. True for the applicant's own research plan (character-limited text boxes, and 'the number of characters allowed for each section includes both spaces and punctuation' is verbatim correct). FALSE as a blanket statement: the Full Proposal ProposalCentral instructions say verbatim 'Your Host Supervisor(s) and Referees must have uploaded their Letters of Reference before the submission deadline, otherwise you will not be able to submit your application', using a mandatory template ('This link includes the Letter of Reference Template that they must use'). And the applicant must use a required downloadable template at BOTH stages — 'Additional information on applicant's publications... The required template for this is available under "Download Template" in the application portal.' So there are required document artefacts in this mechanism; an applicant told 'nothing is uploaded' will not chase their referees' uploads, which is the gating step on the 24 Sep deadline.

The verbatim quotes are correct ('There is one application round per year for the HFSP postdoctoral fellowships'; website 'There is only one competition per year for HFSP Fellowships'), but 'same shape every year' is contradicted by the funder in the very document cited. Sec 4.1 verbatim: 'Application guidelines and criteria may be subject to change each year.' And the AY2027 RECENT CHANGES list shows the cycle did change this year: 'The time of day for all deadlines is now 9:00 am (09:00, Eastern US Time)', the LTF and CDF guidelines were merged into one document, and eligibility rules on host country, nationality, time in host country and lead-author publications were all 'refined'. The day-exact AY2028 projections (~12 Mar / ~5 May / ~12 May / ~24 Sep 2027) therefore rest on a single observed cycle. I could not test them: the AY2026 guidelines PDF 404s at both plausible paths on hfsp.org, and web.archive.org is unreachable from this tool, so no prior-cycle dates could be retrieved. Day-exact projected dates should not be presented as a pattern.

FAQ [B9]: 'The Gilliam award cannot be held concurrently with another extramurally funded fellowship (e.g., NSF GRFP or NIH F31). If awarded, a Fellow would need to relinquish the other award to accept the Gilliam Fellowship. Alternatively, they may defer activation of the Gilliam award by one year.' FAQ [E3]: 'Yes. During the fellowship term, Fellows may not receive funds from other extramurally funded fellowships, scholarships, or similar awards (such as NSF GRFP or NIH F31). If you hold another fellowship at the time of selection, you would need to relinquish it before activating the Gilliam award, or defer Gilliam activation by one year.' MISSING CAVEAT 2, deferring does not pause the obligations: Applicant Guide p.6, verbatim: 'The fellowship term is for up to three consecutive years unless an initial deferment of one year or leave of absence is granted by the fellowship institution and approved by HHMI. There are actually THREE funder documents, and the third breaks the claim's reasoning. The January 2026 EDS Newsletter (p.58), which reprints the 2026 call, states: 'Recipients will be notified in September 2026.' So September is asserted with the CORRECT year in a current-cycle document. The flyer's 'September 2025' is therefore most economically read as a year typo on an intended September 2026 date, not as a carryover from a September-2025 page. Two of three funder documents say September 2026; only the web page says November 2026. 'Prefer the web page' is a defensible tie-break (the web page is the most actively maintained surface and its 2026 dates are otherwise internally consistent), but it is a judgement call, not a settled fact, and the derived claim that the interval is lengthening to ~4 months rests entirely on that one unreconciled line. Also a misquote: the claim attributes 'Monetary awards will be given by December 2026.' to the flyer; the flyer says 'Monetary awards will be given in December.' (no year). That exact sentence with the year is the WEB PAGE's wording. Confirmed within this field: the web page's 'Recipients will be notified by November 2026.', 'Monetary awards will be given by December 2026.', 'Formal award presentations will take place at the EDS Board of Governors Meeting in December 2026.'; the flyer's 'Recipients will be notified in September 2025.'; the IEDM-vs-'EDS Governance meeting' travel-benefit conflict (web page: travel/accommodation 'to attend the IEDM for presentation of an award plaque'; flyer and newsletter: 'to attend the EDS Governance meeting in December 2026 for presentation of the award plaque'); and the copy-paste-error precedent (the archived 2024 page does read 'Monetary awards will be given by December 2023.').

Against it: the live page lists 'Online application form' as item 1 OF THE APPLICATION PACKAGE (i.e. a required component, alongside the letters, bio sketch, statement and transcripts), and the January 2026 Newsletter reprint of the call says 'Completed applications should be submitted online no later than 15 July 2026.' and 'Please submit application online Form'. Prefer the web page (November 2026) as the maintained surface, but flag that two of three funder documents say September.
