refuted.why: The lead framing is wrong and materially so. The claim asserts "the disqualifiers are about career stage and application structure, NOT about holding other grants." The NOFO's own Section V.A RESPONSIVENESS list (verified in the primary PDF, DE-FOA-0003624) contains four overlap-with-other-funding bars that the claim omits entirely: submissions "that have been submitted in response to currently issued ARPA-E NOFOs"; "that are not scientifically distinct from applications submitted in response to currently issued ARPA-E NOFOs"; "that are not distinct in scientific approach or objective from activities currently supported by or actively under consideration for funding by any other office within DOE"; and the same test "by other government agencies or the private sector." These are prior/concurrent-funding disqualifiers, applied at the scope level rather than the award-holding level. A planner told that other grants are irrelevant could submit a concept paper that duplicates an existing DOE- or NSF-funded scope and be screened out before merit review. The two things the claim DID assert under this field (II.D renewal/supplementation ban; one application per PI) are verbatim correct.

Second, smaller defect in the same field: the gloss on 2026 FAQ Q12. The FAQ answer is quoted accurately as far as it goes, but the claim's "i.e. the active award is not itself the bar; proposing to extend it is" is the agent's inference, not the funder's words, and it drops half the answer. ARPA-E's full reply is: "ARPA-E will not pre-assess eligibility for the NOFO. Please review Section II, Eligibility Information, of the NOFO, for all eligibility requirements. Per Section II.D, 'Applicants may not seek renewal or supplementation of their existing awards through this NOFO.' Please also review the Responsiveness criteria in Section V.A." The pointer to V.A is exactly the overlap test the claim says does not exist.

corrections.corrected_value: Two separate bars, not one. (1) AWARD-STRUCTURE BAR, NOFO II.D, verbatim: "ARPA-E is not limiting the number of submissions from a single applicant entity. However, individual PIs may submit no more than one application to this NOFO. ARPA-E will accept only new submissions under this NOFO. Applicants may not seek renewal or supplementation of their existing awards through this NOFO." Holding an active ARPA-E award is not stated to be disqualifying; ARPA-E declines to pre-assess (FAQ Q12). (2) SCOPE-OVERLAP BAR, NOFO V.A RESPONSIVENESS, verbatim bullets: "Submissions that have been submitted in response to currently issued ARPA-E NOFOs." / "Submissions that are not scientifically distinct from applications submitted in response to currently issued ARPA-E NOFOs." / "Submissions that are not distinct in scientific approach or objective from activities currently supported by or actively under consideration for funding by any other office within DOE." / "Submissions that are not distinct in scientific approach or objective from activities currently supported by or actively under consideration for funding by other government agencies or the private sector." Practical rule for a planner: you may hold other grants, but the IGNIITE idea must be scientifically distinct from anything you already have funded, or have pending, anywhere in DOE, at another agency, or in the private sector. Also belongs here as a structural disqualifier (NOFO II.A): "Proposals with multiple co-PIs or project oversight from senior personnel are not eligible for this program." And the career-stage gates (II.A): PhD "within eight years of the Concept Paper deadline, excluding any periods of extended leave" (leave must be stated in the Personal Qualification Summary); U.S. citizen, permanent resident, or Form I-485 filed before Concept Paper submission; at a U.S. IHE, must be a "Tenure-Track Assistant/Associate Professor (i.e., pre-tenured)" at Concept Paper submission — 2026 FAQ Q1: "exceptions will not be considered."

refuted.why: Mischaracterises the single most consequential eligibility line, in the direction that deters eligible applicants. The 2027 RFP p.4 (Eligibility Requirements) reads verbatim: "Candidates who have completed a Burroughs Wellcome Fund career development award (CAMS or CASI) are encouraged to apply but must contact BWF before writing the LOI. Having had BWF travel, career guidance for trainees, preterm birth, regulatory science, or PDEP grants does not impact PATH support." Separately, the concurrent-award clause is not an eligibility rule at all: "Award recipients may not hold concurrent BWF career development awards" sits in TERMS OF GRANT / USE OF FUNDS (2027 RFP p.5) and conditions what an awardee may hold, not what an applicant may apply with. The carve-out half of the claim is correct and verbatim; the blocking half is not. The claim's remaining assertions survive: no NIH-mechanism exclusion appears anywhere in either RFP, and the R01 point is supported by the Importance form instruction (p.8) to describe how the aims "depart from or move beyond currently funded work or, if the first substantial Federal grant has not yet been reached, beyond current proposals."

corrections.corrected_value: Two distinct rules, at two different stages. APPLICATION STAGE (2027 RFP p.4, Eligibility Requirements): a completed BWF career development award (CAMS or CASI) is not disqualifying — "Candidates who have completed a Burroughs Wellcome Fund career development award (CAMS or CASI) are encouraged to apply but must contact BWF before writing the LOI." The pre-LOI contact is mandatory; the application is welcome. Explicitly neutral (no effect on PATH support): BWF travel, career guidance for trainees, preterm birth, regulatory science, and PDEP grants. AWARD STAGE (2027 RFP p.5, Terms of Grant/Use of Funds): "Award recipients may not hold concurrent BWF career development awards." Other-funder support for adjacent work is permitted at award stage: "Award recipients may obtain funds from other sources for research in areas similar to that conducted under these grants, so long as there is no conflict with meeting the BWF award's specific aims." No NIH-mechanism exclusion exists anywhere in the 2026 or 2027 RFP. The real hard bars are seniority, not funding history: applicants "must be 36 months or more from their start date as assistant professors by the LOI deadline of July 16, 2026" (p.3), "Associate professors, with or without tenure, are ineligible" (p.4), and "Candidates who will be promoted to Associate Professor by November 12, 2026 are not eligible to apply" (p.4). NOTE: the 36-month floor is genuinely new for the 2027 cycle — the 2027 RFP cover flags "New Seniority Requirement", whereas the 2026 RFP carried only soft guidance ("In general, faculty in their first 2-3 years are not yet competitive for this award" / "Very few newly appointed assistant professors are competitive"). The claim was right to attribute the hard floor to the 2027 cycle.

result.program_name: NASA Postdoctoral Program (NPP) — Postdoctoral Fellowship (NASA / administered by ORAU)

refuted.why: Refuted as an unqualified universal. apply.html states the pattern and then immediately carves out an exception the claim drops entirely: "Currently, the Astrobiology Program accepts applications only during the March and November rounds, and does not consider applications submitted during the July round." An astrobiology applicant told there are three cycles a year loses a whole round. Separately, the claim calls the cycles "Three fixed cycles per year" while the funder's own word on apply.html is "typically" ("Annual application cycle deadlines ... are typically March 1, July 1, and November 1"). Source: https://npp.orau.org/applicants/apply.html

Unsupported sub-claim: "The application portal is open continuously between cycles." No such statement found on any NPP page. What the funder actually says is narrower: "You may return and edit the application up until the current deadline" (apply.html) and "Applications can be altered up to the current cycle deadline" (faq.html). Neither asserts continuous between-cycle openness. Sources: https://npp.orau.org/applicants/apply.html , https://npp.orau.org/applicants/faq.html

The forward dates "March 1, 2027, then July 1, 2027" are NOT published anywhere on npp.orau.org as dated deadlines — only the current cycle (November 1, 2026) is dated on the homepage. They are the agent's projection from a pattern the funder hedges as "typically", and the July 2027 round does not exist for the Astrobiology Program. Presenting them at the same confidence as the verified November date is the drift risk. (The November 1, 2026 date itself is fully confirmed — see corrections.)

Sub-item 3 is wrong as stated on two counts. (i) It presents official transcripts as a universal requirement; apply.html says "Postdoctoral Fellow applicants are required to upload their official doctoral degree transcripts" and explicitly "Applicants for Senior Fellowships are not required to provide transcripts." (ii) "Official transcripts must be ordered from the degree-granting institution (self-downloaded records are rejected)" overstates the rule: "A transcript labeled 'Unofficial' or 'Issued to Student' by the academic institution will be accepted as long as it meets all four of the requirements listed above; however, student academic records downloaded/obtained by the applicant or by academic advisors from internal institutional systems will not be accepted." So an institution-issued 'Unofficial' transcript is acceptable. Source: https://npp.orau.org/applicants/apply.html

"Hard threshold: 'applicants must receive an overall score of 75 (out of 100) or greater to be eligible'" misquotes by deletion. process.html reads: "Typically, applicants must receive an overall score of 75 (out of 100) or greater to be eligible for selection into the program. However, final decisions regarding selectability based on an applicant's score are at the discretion of the NASA selection organization (center, facility, host organization)." The claim drops both "Typically" and the discretion sentence, converting a soft guideline into a hard cut-off. Source: https://npp.orau.org/applicants/process.html

"No NPP-specific resubmission policy is published" is refuted. process.html publishes one, verbatim: "Applications can be resubmitted by the applicant for consideration in the next application cycle. An applicant may submit a revised version of their previously submitted application at any time before the deadline." Applicants are also "provided the review results so that perceived strengths and weaknesses of the application can be assessed." The narrower sub-claims (no A1/A2 designation, no introduction page, no response-to-reviewers requirement, no stated cap on attempts) are not contradicted anywhere I could find and stand. Source: https://npp.orau.org/applicants/process.html

Not wrong on what it says, but materially incomplete on the field's own stated purpose ("getting this wrong tells an ineligible person to waste months"). It omits an outright disqualifier published on faq.html: "Researchers who are affiliated with an institution in the People's Republic of China (PRC) or who intend to collaborate with researchers in the PRC are not eligible for an NPP award." It also omits the residency bar on eligibility.html: "Establishing and maintaining residency at the Center or at the location of the advisor is required to begin the appointment and to remain in the program." Sources: https://npp.orau.org/applicants/faq.html , https://npp.orau.org/applicants/eligibility.html

The portal/NSPIRES reasoning is correct (Zintellect confirmed; NSPIRES and Grants.gov appear nowhere in NPP application material), but the field as supplied omits the single most drift-sensitive required-document fact on the whole mechanism — the proposal page limit and its penalty. See corrections for the verbatim text that must be added.

corrections.corrected_value: CONFIRMED — do not strip this date. Verified today (2026-09-18) on the funder's own homepage, https://npp.orau.org/ , not via a search index. Site-wide alert banner: "November 2026 cycle is open. View current opportunities". Body text verbatim: "November 2026 application cycle is now open" and "Application deadline is Sunday, November 1, 2026 at 6 p.m. U.S. Eastern Time." Independent check: 1 November 2026 is in fact a Sunday, so the funder's own day-of-week is internally consistent. The 6 p.m. ET cut-off (vs. the 11:59 p.m. ET ROSES habit) is confirmed on the same page and is worth surfacing prominently. Show this date. Present the two following rounds as pattern rather than as dated facts: "then typically March 1 and July 1 (funder's wording: 'typically'; the Astrobiology Program skips the July round)."

Corrected wording: "Three cycles a year — the funder's own words are 'Annual application cycle deadlines for the NASA Postdoctoral Program are typically March 1, July 1, and November 1' (apply.html) and 'Annual NASA Postdoctoral Program application deadlines are March 1, July 1, and November 1' (about/index.html). Exception, stated by the funder: 'Currently, the Astrobiology Program accepts applications only during the March and November rounds, and does not consider applications submitted during the July round.' Cut-off time is 6 p.m. U.S. Eastern Time (stated on the homepage for the current cycle). You may edit a filed application up until the current deadline; there is no published statement that the portal is open between cycles." The NPMP (management) track follows the same cycle: "NPMP application cycles follow the same cycle as the NPRP (March 1, July 1, and November 1)."

MUST ADD (verbatim, apply.html and tips.html): "The maximum length for the proposal is 15 pages, including figures and citations; double-spaced; 12-point font; one-inch margins. Important: your proposal may be returned without review if it does not conform to these formatting instructions." Proposal has six required sections; the abstract of goals is "maximum one page". Uploaded as PDF. Transcript mechanics: PDF only, no password/certificate, "Maximum file size is 10MB", English or an official English translation, all pages legible, and the applicant must redact SSN/national ID, date of birth, place of birth, parents' names and student ID from ALL pages of ALL documents. Transcript checklist requires all four listed Registrar's-Office elements. International applicants whose institution cannot produce a conforming transcript submit a signed statement/certificate instead. Portal mechanics confirmed: Zintellect ("Zintellect, the applicant portal, will guide you through the application process"); re-upload of the proposal file is allowed any number of times before the deadline; submission is by the applicant pressing "Submit Application" — no AOR, no SAM/UEI, no Grants.gov.

Core claim stands: no LOI, no pre-proposal, no Step-1 stage found anywhere. Corrected/expanded pre-deadline chain: (1) Three letters of recommendation due AT the deadline — confirmed verbatim on both tips.html and apply.html. Two constraints the claim omits and that break plans: "If you are applying as a Postdoctoral Fellow (i.e., you have received your doctoral degree within the last five years), one reference must be from your thesis advisor" AND "the NASA research opportunity advisor shall not serve as a reference, even if he or she was your thesis advisor." (2) Advisor contact — confirmed ("highly recommended", tips.html), but the claim understates it: the advisor is a GATE, not just 20% of the score. process.html: "Proposals that are recommended by the advisor, move on to the external review phase." (3) Transcripts — required only of Postdoctoral Fellow applicants (doctorate held <5 years); Senior Fellowship applicants are not required to provide them; institution-issued 'Unofficial'/'Issued to Student' transcripts are acceptable if they carry all four checklist elements. One-per-cycle rule (quoted by the claim as FAQ) actually appears on apply.html verbatim as: "Note: You may submit only ONE application for ONE research opportunity per application cycle."

All timing quotes verified verbatim on process.html: notification "approximately two to three months after the application deadline"; review results "typically available within two to three months after the application deadline"; accept/decline "generally within three weeks of receipt" and "If an award is not accepted within three weeks of receipt, it will be regarded as declined and may be offered to another applicant"; pending status "remain eligible for an NPP award for one (1) additional cycle from the application deadline"; criteria 40/20/20/20 exactly as quoted. Machinery corrected: stage 1 is the NASA Center advisor's review (a gate — only recommended proposals advance); stage 2 is "three well-qualified, external reviewers" who, "In cases of significant disagreement ... will meet virtually to discuss the application and come to a consensus"; then "the results of the external panel review are ... communicated to the respective NASA Center, and the Center decides on the award of fellowships." Score line must read: "Typically, applicants must receive an overall score of 75 (out of 100) or greater to be eligible for selection into the program. However, final decisions regarding selectability ... are at the discretion of the NASA selection organization." Start date confirmed on fellows/index.html: "The Fellow's appointment start date should normally be within six (6) months of the date of the ORAU offer letter"; the anticipated start date "is approved by the NPP advisor", and any CHANGE "must be approved by the NPP advisor and the NPP Center representative, and ORAU must be notified." The claim's exclusion of DAPR / SPD-09D / the 150-day rule is correct — none appear in NPP material.

Both quoted bars are verbatim-correct on eligibility.html: "You must not have held an NPP appointment for five years prior to applying. NPP Fellows are eligible for another award five years after the end of the previous appointment" and "Fellows may not provide services for compensation to a third party, or supplement their stipends through simultaneous employment, grants, or other sources of income that compete with the fellowship." The clock-from-END reading is supported. ADD three things: (a) PRC bar — "Researchers who are affiliated with an institution in the People's Republic of China (PRC) or who intend to collaborate with researchers in the PRC are not eligible for an NPP award" (faq.html); (b) residency — relocation to the Center (or, for virtual centers such as the NASA Astrobiology Program, to the advisor's university location) is "required to begin the appointment and to remain in the program" (eligibility.html); (c) DISAMBIGUATE the two different five-year clocks, which this field currently invites readers to confuse: the five-year NPP-appointment bar above is an ELIGIBILITY bar, whereas the other published five-year line is only a ROUTING rule — "A Postdoctoral Fellow has held the doctoral degree for less than five years at the time of application. A Senior Fellow has held the doctoral degree for five or more years at the time of application." A doctorate older than five years bars nobody; it changes which track you apply on (and removes the transcript requirement). Related appointment fact: "An NPP fellowship term of appointment is initially for 24 months ... NPP appointments are limited to three years. Year 3 must be funded by the advisor and approved by the Center."

Not refuted — I independently found no published NPP funded proposals, sample proposals, or selection abstracts on npp.orau.org, and the NSPIRES-abstract route genuinely does not apply (NPP is not a ROSES element and is not submitted through NSPIRES). The nearest usable substitutes on the funder's own site, which the field should point a first-time applicant to instead of leaving them empty-handed: the searchable research-opportunity catalogue (each listing states the science goals a proposal must address and names the NASA advisor to contact), and the Current/Former Fellows pages, which show who was funded, at which Center, and on what topic. Beyond that: not found.

On the framing question of whether a dated deadline may be shown: nothing in the verification refutes showing it here. The November 1, 2026, 6 p.m. ET date is stated by the funder on its own homepage, is internally consistent (1 Nov 2026 is a Sunday), and was read today from npp.orau.org rather than from a search index — it meets the showable bar. The defensible rule is not "no dates" but "no undated dates": show a date only with the funder page it came from and the date it was read, and downgrade PROJECTED future rounds (March/July 2027 here) to pattern language, since the funder itself writes "typically" and carves out Astrobiology from the July round. Recommended surface for a PhD-student/postdoc reader: the dated current deadline, the 6 p.m. ET cut-off called out against the 11:59 p.m. ET habit, the ~6-weeks-out letters-of-recommendation trigger, and the advisor-contact step as step one.

refuted.why: REFUTED AS INCOMPLETE on exactly the axis the task flags as high-stakes: the claim lists only disqualifiers and states NO carve-outs. The NOFO's very next section is a carve-out, and it is the one an applicant most needs: 'Concurrent grants from other organizations -- You may simultaneously hold fellowships or grants from institutions other than NEH -- including sabbaticals and grants from your own institution -- in support of the same project during your period of performance.' As written, the claim would tell a faculty member holding a sabbatical or an internal research grant that they are conflicted out. It also omits a fourth disqualifier that IS in the same NOFO section: 'You may not serve as the project director or key personnel on an NEH institutional award while working full time on an NEH individual award.' Separately, a verbatim-presented quote is misquoted: the claim says the programme announcement repeats 'You may not hold any other NEH individual award...' verbatim. It does not. The HBCU Program Announcement reads 'You may not ACCEPT OR hold any other NEH individual award, including a Chairman's Award to Individuals, in the same federal fiscal year.' The NOFO omits 'accept or'; the announcement adds it. The claim's substantive point (it is a programme rule, not just boilerplate) survives; the quote does not.

REFUTED AS TRUNCATED on a page-limit claim. The claim's page-limit list breaks off after 'Narrative -- narrative.pdf -- required -- 3 pages, and'. The narrative figure is correct ('Your narrative must not exceed three single-spaced pages'), and the surrounding claims (FON 20260422-HB, FAL 45.160, individual applicant of record, tracking number beginning HB, no budget required, citations counted, non-PDF auto-rejected) all verify, but a partial page-limit table is the failure mode this field exists to prevent -- an applicant reading it would not know the resume cap or that a confirmation of institutional support is needed at all. Corrected full list supplied below. Also worth noting: the claim asserts the tracking number begins 'HB' without noting the NOFO gives four prefixes across the combined programmes ('a tracking number beginning with FEL, FO, FZ, or HB'); HB is correct for this programme.

corrections.corrected_value: DISQUALIFIERS (NEH Individual Programs NOFO, 'Limitations regarding other NEH awards', verbatim): (1) 'You may not hold any other NEH individual award, including a Chairman's Award to Individuals, in the same federal fiscal year.' -- the HBCU Program Announcement states this as 'You may not ACCEPT OR hold any other NEH individual award...'; (2) 'You may not hold two or more NEH individual awards with overlapping periods of performance or in support of the same activities. NEH will not delay the period of performance beyond the stated timelines of the Program Announcement to accommodate overlapping individual awards.'; (3) 'You may not apply for activities for which you previously received NEH funding.'; (4) 'You may not serve as the project director or key personnel on an NEH institutional award while working full time on an NEH individual award.' Plus, from 'Resubmissions and multiple submissions': 'You may not submit more than one application for a NEH individual award at the same deadline. For example, you may not apply for a Fellowship and Public Scholars award in the same year.' -- binding in 2027 because all four individual programmes share the 4/14/27 deadline. CARVE-OUT (NOFO, 'Concurrent grants from other organizations', verbatim): 'You may simultaneously hold fellowships or grants from institutions other than NEH -- including sabbaticals and grants from your own institution -- in support of the same project during your period of performance.' Also permissive: you may apply while working as part of a collaborative team if seeking funding only for yourself, each collaborator submitting a separate application.

Page limits, taken from the announcement's per-attachment body text (the layout of the summary table extracts with scrambled column alignment, so the body text is the reliable source): 1 Narrative, narrative.pdf, required -- 'must not exceed three single-spaced pages'; no executive summary, cover page, headers or table of contents; images/charts/diagrams allowed inside the limit. 2 Work plan, workplan.pdf, required -- 'must not exceed one page'. 3 Bibliography, bibliography.pdf, required -- 'must not exceed one page'. 4 Resume, resume.pdf, required -- 'must not exceed two pages'. 5 Confirmation of institutional support, confirmation.pdf -- recommended at time of application, REQUIRED in order to receive funding ('NEH will not issue your award without a letter of [institutional support]'); on letterhead, signed by an institutional representative. 6 Editions and translations sample, translation.pdf, conditionally required -- 'Do not exceed two pages total (original and translation)'. 7 Visual materials, visual.pdf, recommended -- 'Do not exceed one page'; must be PDF, not .jpg. 8 Data sample, datasample.pdf, conditionally required -- 'Do not exceed one page'. 9 Data management plan, datamanagement.pdf, conditionally required. 10 Degree conferral, degreeconferral.pdf, conditionally required. 11 Explanation of delinquent federal debt, delinquentdebt.pdf, conditionally required. Formatting: letter size, 1-inch margins, single-spaced, readable font no smaller than 11 pt, 'any standard citation style is acceptable; citations are included in page counts', 'Attachments in non-PDF format (Word, etc.) will result in an application being automatically rejected.' Four Grants.gov forms: SF-424 Individual, NEH Supplemental Information for Individuals, Project/Performance Site Location(s), Attachments. Budget: 'You are not required to submit a budget.' (NOFO). Tracking number: 'When NEH receives your application, the agency will assign it a tracking number beginning with FEL, FO, FZ, or HB' -- HB for this programme.

The claim calls the reference-letter date a due date. Soften it: the Program Announcement says 'To ensure full consideration, letters of reference must be submitted online no later than June 4, 2026' -- and the NOFO adds the escape hatch the claim omits: 'NEH accepts letters after the deadline, and late letters will be added to your application. However, it is possible that reviewers will not take them into account.' So a late letter does not invalidate the application; it risks going unread. Everything else in the field verifies verbatim: 'Approximately two to three weeks after the deadline, NEH will email your letter writers, asking them to submit their letters online by the date specified in the Program Announcement', the mid-cycle amendment ('Published March 2, 2026 / Updated (amend reference letter deadline) April 1, 2026'), and the two-letters requirement (with the extra rule that for a translation project one letter must come from a language expert who assesses the sample). The 2027 letter deadline is indeed not yet published -- correctly reported as not found.

Confirmed, with one wording caveat worth carrying. The programme page's dates block renders the last field as 'Project start date: April 1, 2028 | September 1, 2029' -- two dates with a separator, with no explicit 'to' or 'between' on the page itself. The window reading is nonetheless right, corroborated by the prior cycle's announcement, which spells it out: 'Projects must start between April 1, 2027, and September 1, 2028.' Flag it as a window inferred from the page's date-field rendering plus last cycle's wording, not from 2027 prose -- NEH has not published the 2027 announcement. Everything else verifies verbatim in the NOFO: 'approximately 9-12 months after the application deadline. This is not an authorization to begin performance or incur related costs. Successful applicants will be required to complete the NEH Individual Programs Acceptance Form, from which NEH will determine your payment schedule.'; 'The National Council meets at least twice each year to review applications and advise the NEH Chairman. By law, the Chairman has the sole authority to make final funding decisions.'; 'Award decisions are discretionary and are not appealable to any federal official or board.'; and the OGM risk assessment, which 'confirm[s] the applicant's continued eligibility'. refuted.why: MOST SERIOUS FINDING. All three quoted sentences are verbatim-accurate, and the claim is right that there is no prior-K/prior-R01 exclusion. But the claim frames the sole disqualifier as CURRENTLY HOLDING or HAVING ACCEPTED another postdoctoral fellowship. The funder's own Pre-award TA slide deck (Final-Pre-TA-slides-RFA-27-12-9-25.pdf, slide 5, 'Eligibility by Type of Grant / NJCCR Postdoctoral Fellowship Grant') states a materially BROADER bar the claim omits entirely: 'Applicants who have previously completed a postdoctoral fellowship are not eligible.' Past completion, not just current or accepted. The same slide also says 'This fellowship may not overlap with any other training fellowships' — ANY training fellowship, not only a postdoctoral one. The claim's framing would tell a researcher who already finished a postdoc fellowship elsewhere that they are clear to apply, when the funder's own applicant-facing deck says they are not. That is exactly the failure mode flagged in attack vector (b). The claim also omits two further RFA-stated conflicts: 'NJCCR grant recipients whose grant period is ongoing and will overlap with the RFA 2027 grant period are not eligible to apply' (RFA p.2), and the stipend rule that institutional supplements 'may not come from other full-time fellowship awards or from NJCCR funds' (RFA p.5).

Over-claimed. The FY2027 shape is fully confirmed verbatim, and 'Multi-year awards are made through one-year contracts. Each funding award within the funded period will be contingent upon the availability of funds and Progress Reports' is verbatim from RFA p.9. I could not retrieve any prior-cycle dated timeline from the funder: njccr-rfa-2023.pdf, -2024, -2025 and -2026 ALL return HTTP 404, and the grants page lists only 2027 materials. result.program_name: NSF Astronomy and Astrophysics Postdoctoral Fellowships (AAPF) — National Science Foundation

refuted.why: Not refuted on substance, but the sourcing is wrong and the claim is presented as if it came from this mechanism's own documents. I fetched NSF 22-621 directly and asked specifically for resubmission language: the solicitation does NOT address resubmission of declined proposals or whether a revised proposal is treated as new. The quoted strings ('A declined proposal may be resubmitted, but only after it has undergone substantial revision'; 'The Foundation will treat the revised proposal as a new proposal') are agency-wide PAPPG text, not AAPF text. More importantly, the claim omits the interaction that actually matters here: because 'a proposer may not participate in more than two AAPF competitions' (verbatim, confirmed on both the opportunity page and the solicitation), a resubmission is not a free retry — it consumes your second and final lifetime attempt. The mitigating carve-out, also verbatim from the solicitation and absent from the claim: 'Proposals that are not reviewed (i.e., withdrawn before review or returned without review) do not count toward the two-competition limit.'

corrections.corrected_value: Confirmed as to every date, wording and day-of-week, against the funder's own page (fetched directly, not via a search index). NSF opportunity page verbatim: 'August 15 - October 15, 2026 (Window)' / 'August 15 - October 15, Annually Thereafter' / 'Due by 5pm submitting organization's local time'. Program Status on that page reads 'Active'; Solicitation Number 'NSF 22-621'. The Updates page returns a page with an empty main content area — no notice, cancellation, pause or deadline change. Day-of-week checks pass: 15 Oct 2026 is a Thursday; the projected 2027 instance 15 Aug (Sunday) - 15 Oct (Friday) is arithmetically right. FY2026 awards confirm the competition actually runs: NSF awards API returns award 2602368 issued 07 May 2026 at $330,000, plus nine more issued 07-21 May 2026, all titled 'Postdoctoral Fellowship: AAPF: ...'. ONE DURABILITY FIX, not a factual one: drop the embedded countdown ('27 days from today'). It is arithmetically correct for 2026-09-18 and silently wrong every day after. Keep the rule plus the dated instance; the rule is what does not rot.

Both halves confirmed verbatim, and the negative is confirmed too: I asked the solicitation directly whether holding prior or current research funding disqualifies an applicant, and it contains no such restriction. Confirmed limits: 'Each proposer may submit only one AAPF proposal per annual competition. In addition, a proposer may not participate in more than two AAPF competitions.' And 'No additional appointment or fellowship may be held during the period of the fellowship. No other remuneration from any source may be accepted during the period of the fellowship without permission from the cognizant NSF Program Officer.' TWO ADDITIONS the claim leaves out, both of which gate eligibility harder than prior funding does. (1) The carve-out on the lifetime cap, verbatim: 'Proposals that are not reviewed (i.e., withdrawn before review or returned without review) do not count toward the two-competition limit.' (2) The actual disqualifiers, verbatim: 'The proposer has earned the doctoral degree in an appropriate scientific field within five (5) years prior to the proposal submission deadline or will complete the doctoral degree by 1 October following the proposal deadline' and 'The proposer is a citizen, national, or lawful permanent resident (Green Card Holder) of the United States.' The citizenship bar is the one that most often sends an otherwise strong candidate away, and it was missing entirely.

The headline claim is confirmed verbatim ('Fellowship proposals must be submitted by the Fellowship candidate, not by the Fellowship candidate's current or proposed organizational Sponsored Projects Office (SPO)'; candidate serves as own SPO and AOR). But the field was truncated mid-sentence and, critically, states NO PAGE LIMITS. The solicitation gives them explicitly: 'The Project Description must be no more than ten (10) single-spaced pages in length' and 'The Project Summary: This section must be no more than one page in length.' Also missing: the host institution letter is not a generic letter — it must be signed by the department chair and the proposed mentor. Add both; a page limit is the single most drift-sensitive required-document fact and its absence here is the biggest gap in the whole record.

Confirmed: solicitation states LOI and preliminary proposal are not required, and I independently asked it for any mention of reference letters or referee-submitted letters — it has none. The adjacent point stands: the host institution letter and letters of collaboration are candidate-uploaded proposal components with no separate due date. Confirmed addition: the host institution letter must carry the signatures of the department chair AND the proposed mentor, and letters of collaboration are required from educational partners. That is a two-signature long-lead item, which sharpens rather than changes the claim's own advice.

Confirmed on the funder's own text: notification 'on or about 1 February following the proposal submission deadline'; tenure 'must begin on or before 1 October following'; up to 36 months at $110,000/yr ($75,000 stipend + $35,000 allowance, a breakdown the claim omits), 48-month outer envelope, non-renewable. refuted.why: The flat claim "No A1 designation, no cap, no window" is wrong on two of three counts. (1) NO WINDOW is contradicted by PAPPG 24-1 Ch. NSF programs that accept proposals at any time may have established guidelines in which a declined proposal (or reasonable facsimile of that proposal/topic by the same PI, and co-PIs, where applicable) is ineligible for resubmission for a specified period of time." That moratorium clause is aimed precisely at the accept-anytime hosts the claim recommends. (2) NO CAP is contradicted by both host solicitations the claim itself nominates, each of which names GOALI explicitly. NSF 26-519 (MPS Chemistry), verbatim: "Limit on Number of Proposals per PI or Co-PI: 2 ... Beginning Sept. 1, 2026, and annually thereafter, no more than two proposals per year may list the same individual as either PI, co-PI or senior/key personnel ... If two proposals list the same individual as PI, co-PI or senior/key personnel, at least one of those proposals must be a multi-investigator or collaborative proposal. Any proposals submitted after reaching the two-proposal limit will be returned by NSF without review. Declined proposals can be resubmitted in the same one-year period in which they were submitted, if major revisions are made and the annual submission limit described above has not been exceeded. ... These restrictions also cover the following funding opportunities: Grant Opportunities for Academic Liaison with Industry (GOALI)". NSF 26-521 (MPS Materials) is harsher, verbatim: "Limit on Number of Proposals per PI or co-PI: 1 ... Beginning October 1 of each year, no more than one proposal per fiscal year may list the same individual as either PI or co-PI ... NSF will return without review any subsequent proposals submitted during the same fiscal year ... This restriction also applies to proposals submitted to the following funding opportunities: Grant Opportunities for Academic Liaison with Industry (GOALI)". Only "no A1 designation" survives. For an applicant this is the single most consequential error in the set: it turns "Proposals Accepted Anytime, so submit whenever" into a one-shot-per-fiscal-year decision in materials, and a two-shot decision in chemistry with a collaboration string attached.

Two defects. (a) STALE PAGE-LIMIT CLAIM: "2-page DMSP now a Research.gov webform" is half right and half stale. PAPPG 24-1 Supplement 2 (NSF 26-202, issued and effective Jan 22, 2026) revises Ch. II.D.2.(i).(ii) so the DMSP is "created using the tool implemented on Research.gov" and STRIKES the previous text "a document of no more than two pages uploaded under 'Data Management and Sharing Plan' in the supplementary documentation section of Research.gov." The two-page cap is removed, not retained; the note also fixes the tool's release at April 27, 2026, before which a PDF upload applied. (b) The field as delivered is TRUNCATED mid-sentence ("The IHE-industry interaction should be described i") and therefore cannot be judged complete; in the portion visible it does not carry the one GOALI-specific REQUIRED DOCUMENT, which is the hardest failure mode here (see corrections).

corrections.corrected_value: Add the mandatory GOALI document and the collaborative-proposal bar, both verbatim from PAPPG 24-1 Ch. corrections.corrected_value: The SBIR/STTR bar and the three small-business criteria are correct and verbatim from NSF's own ENG GOALI page, and PAPPG II.F.5 says the same in slightly different words ("with the exception of small businesses that meet these requirements and are not currently funded NSF SBIR/STTR recipients"). The proposal must disclose any financial interest that the PI, co-PI, other senior/key personnel and/or IHE have in the small business partner and identify appropriate mitigation of any financial conflict of interest." Correct framing: NSF-wide, PAPPG 24-1 Ch. IV.E applies unchanged — "A declined proposal may be resubmitted, but only after it has undergone substantial revision"; "A resubmitted proposal that has not clearly taken into account the major comments or concerns resulting from the prior NSF review may be returned without review"; "The Foundation will treat the revised proposal as a new proposal, subject to the standard review procedures." Upload this statement under single-copy documents. Proposals that have not been substantially revised will be returned without review."

Everything material checks out; three small refinements. Full proposals are accepted anytime starting September 1, 2026" — and it does cover exactly nine chemistry programs (Chemical Catalysis, Chemical Measurement and Imaging, Chemical Mechanism Function and Properties, Chemical Structure and Dynamics, Chemical Synthesis, Chemical Systems and Solutions, Chemical Theory Models and Computational Methods, Chemistry of Life Processes, Macromolecular Supramolecular and Nanochemistry), superseding NSF 22-605/22-606. result.program_name: NSF Graduate Research Fellowship Program (GRFP)

refuted.why: The claim states the binding constraint is career stage and prior degrees, "not prior grant funding." REFUTED by the funder's own solicitation NSF 26-526, which contains an explicit concurrent-funding bar: "An individual may not accept the Graduate Research Fellowship if the individual accepts or is supported by another federal graduate fellowship." This is exactly the class of error the check targets: a dual NDSEG/DOE-CSGF/NIH-fellowship winner reading this field would not learn they must choose. Second defect: the field frames disqualification around degrees EARNED, but NSF's applicant fact sheet (GRFP-Applicant-Overview.pdf p.5, ineligible column) lists "Previous enrollment in a graduate degree program (non-degree courses not counted)" — prior enrollment without a completed degree can also disqualify. The claim's own proposed correction to eligibility_notes ("in any field", not "in a GRFP-eligible field") is itself CONFIRMED verbatim on nsf.gov/funding/initiatives/grfp/eligibility and in the FAQ.

The headline answer (no LOI, no preliminary proposal) is CONFIRMED verbatim in NSF 26-526: "Letters of Intent: Not applicable" and "Preliminary Proposal Submission: Not applicable". But the load-bearing sub-claim — "letters gate SUBMISSION, not just review" — is REFUTED by NSF's own current FAQ: "You can still submit your application, but it will not be reviewed without at least two letters." The references page does say "Applicants will be unable to submit applications without the required number of reference letters," so two current NSF pages contradict each other; the claim presented the stronger one as settled fact without flagging the conflict. The corrected, conflict-free statement is in corrections.

corrections.corrected_value: Two constraints, not one. (1) CAREER STAGE / PRIOR DEGREES (primary, as claimed): ineligible are "Individuals who have earned a master's, doctoral, or terminal degree in any field" (eligibility page); FAQ: "If you have a master's degree, you are not eligible." ADD: the applicant fact sheet also lists "Previous enrollment in a graduate degree program (non-degree courses not counted)" as disqualifying — enrollment, not only a completed degree. (2) CONCURRENT FEDERAL FELLOWSHIP BAR (omitted by the claim, must be added): NSF 26-526, verbatim — "An individual may not accept the Graduate Research Fellowship if the individual accepts or is supported by another federal graduate fellowship." No parallel bar on non-federal fellowships or on research assistantships appears in the solicitation; do not assert one. Note NSF does allow Reserve status (see the May 2027 "Declaration of Tenure/Reserve" step) as the mechanism for a Fellow holding another award in a given year.

result.program_name: NVIDIA Graduate Fellowship Program (NVIDIA)

refuted.why: Framing is wrong on the one question that actually matters to a student who already holds funding. The claim presents this field as "unusually permissive, and all quoted" and lists only carve-outs (repeat awards, current fellow may reapply, no per-university/per-team cap, prior internship an asset). All four quotes check out verbatim on the live funder page, but the claim omits the single restrictive term on that page, which sits in Terms and Conditions: "Whether it is OK to combine the NVIDIA fellowship with another fellowship depends on several factors -- please contact the NVIDIA Graduate Fellowship for details on this matter." That is conditional and unresolved, not permissive. It also omits three other money-side constraints that decide whether a currently-funded student can take the award at all: "Amount of the award cannot exceed stipend, tuition, and mandatory fees", "We require that no overhead or indirect costs are charged to the award", and "There may also be university-specific restrictions that pertain." A GRFP/Hertz/NDSEG holder reading the claim as written would conclude concurrent holding is fine; the funder says ask us. (Verified by live render of https://research.nvidia.com/graduate-fellowships on 2026-09-18.)

Two of its specifics are not supported by any source. (1) "Fixed mid-September close" is a pattern asserted from a single observed dated cycle: the live page carries exactly two dates, both 15 September 2025 (student 3pm PT, letters 12noon PT), and the recipient pages (2026, 2025, 2024, 2023-2002) publish names only, no prior deadlines. Annual cadence IS supported ("You can apply each year you are enrolled full-time until the year before you complete your PhD"), but "fixed mid-September" across cycles is unverified here -- WebSearch budget was exhausted for this session too and web.archive.org is unavailable, so no multi-year cross-check was possible. (2) "Portal opens over the summer" appears nowhere on the funder page; the page never states when the submission portal opens. Treat both as inference, not funder text. The rest of the timeline (letters 3 hours before the student deadline; review ~8 weeks; notification by end of November; 3-4 month in-person internship; 9-month award year) is verbatim-correct.

The verbatim reapplication quote is correct ("Yes. You can apply each year you are enrolled full-time until the year before you complete your PhD. You can follow the same guidelines and application process as any new applicant."), and no resubmission track or response-to-reviewers component exists. But "no feedback given to unsuccessful applicants" is not stated anywhere on the funder page -- it is an unsourced negative and should be marked not found rather than asserted. The claim also misses the one thing the page does offer an unsuccessful applicant, which is actionable: "Applicants may choose to opt-in for an internship evaluation outside of the fellowship (in the event the applicant is not chosen for an award.)"

corrections.corrected_value: CONFIRMED as stated, and the claim's own flagged ambiguity can now be partly resolved. Live render of https://research.nvidia.com/graduate-fellowships on 2026-09-18 (rendering browser; WebFetch of the same URL agrees) shows no 2026-dated deadline anywhere: a regex sweep of the rendered body returns the year tokens 2026, 2025, 2024, 2023, 2002, 2027 only, and the only two September sentences on the page are both 2025 -- "the deadline for recommendation letters is 12noon Pacific Time, September 15, 2025" and "Submit the final application when all items are complete, and prior to the application deadline: 3pm Pacific Time, September 15, 2025." The DOM detail also checks out: the page contains exactly one anchor matching submission/closed/apply/portal, text "Submissions are now CLOSED", with href="" (empty) -- so that line is indeed the dormant apply control and watching that one page is sound advice. RESOLUTION OF THE AMBIGUITY the claim could not settle: the posted Sept-2025 text belongs to a cycle that has already been decided, not to a live round. The site has published https://research.nvidia.com/graduate-fellowships/2026 -- "We are excited to announce the 2026 NVIDIA Graduate Fellowship recipients!" (10 fellows named, plus 4 finalists) -- and the programme intro says "This is the twenty-fifth year that NVIDIA has invited PhD students to submit their research projects", which matches 25 classes 2002-2026 inclusive (the Fellows tabs read 2026 / 2025 / 2024 / 2023-2002). So the Sept-2025 round produced the already-announced 2026 class and the application section simply was never rolled over; https://research.nvidia.com/graduate-fellowships/2027 returns HTTP 404. What remains genuinely unknown: whether a mid-September 2026 round for AY2027-2028 ran quietly and is unreflected on the page. I could not rule that out (WebSearch budget exhausted for this session; web.archive.org unavailable). Correct actionable line for a user: no dated next deadline is published; plan against a mid-September close, have recommenders lined up by late August, and check this one page from July onward.

Split the field. PERMISSIVE AND QUOTED (all verified verbatim on the funder page): repeat awards -- "At this time there is no limit on the number of times you can be awarded the NVIDIA Graduate Fellowship Award. Keep in mind you can only receive one per year!"; current fellows may reapply -- "Yes. You can apply each year you are enrolled full-time until the year before you complete your PhD."; no institutional cap -- "there is no limit per University nor is there a limit per graduate team provided the research is different and interesting to NVIDIA"; a prior NVIDIA internship is an asset the page invites you to cite -- "Have you ever interned with NVIDIA before? If so, let us know what you worked on during that time." CONDITIONAL, MUST BE STATED: "Whether it is OK to combine the NVIDIA fellowship with another fellowship depends on several factors -- please contact the NVIDIA Graduate Fellowship for details on this matter." FINANCIAL CEILING AND ADMIN CONSTRAINTS: "The amount of the award is based on the individual student's actual costs of stipend, tuition and mandatory fees"; "Amount of the award cannot exceed stipend, tuition, and mandatory fees"; "We require that no overhead or indirect costs are charged to the award"; "Awards are not transferable to another student"; "Awards are issued to the university for disbursement, not directly to the student"; "There may also be university-specific restrictions that pertain." HARD DISQUALIFIERS (these, not prior funding, are what actually excludes people): "Full-time NVIDIA employees and immediate family of NVIDIA employees cannot participate"; first year of PhD not yet completed at time of application; not enrolled full-time through the 9-month award year / expecting to graduate before May/June of the award year's end; unable to do the in-person summer internship. OUTSIDE WORK: part-time work during the fellowship is allowed only if "the work is beneficial to the progress of your PhD, you remain full-time enrolled at your institution, and a conflict of interest does not exist between NVIDIA and the other entity". Source: live render of https://research.nvidia.com/graduate-fellowships, 2026-09-18.

refuted.why: Overstates references as a required, load-bearing element. The funder's FAQ/Application page states verbatim: "This year's application does not require references." The Application-Evaluation-Award page lists "Up to 3 References" as "Highly Recommended but not required." The ordering rule the claim quotes IS real and confirmed verbatim ("Your references must complete their recommendations BEFORE you submit your application"), but it governs an OPTIONAL element. Calling it "THE HIDDEN LONG-LEAD ITEM that functions like an LOI deadline" and instructing applicants to treat "ask your three referees" as a hard task due 3-4 weeks out misrepresents an optional component as mandatory. The genuine completeness gate ("If for any reason an application does not contain all of the required elements, it will not be reviewed") does not bite on missing references.

The sentence "There is no prior-award exclusion anywhere in the eligibility criteria" is false as written. The Eligibility page itself carries a funding restriction: "Fellow may not accept simultaneous remuneration from another fellowship, e.g., if an applicant is offered both an NSF and an NDSEG Fellowship, the applicant must choose between the two offers." The claim's substantive point survives (the bar is on acceptance, not on applying), but the restriction is located on the eligibility page, not absent from it. The claim also omits a materially decisive fact for anyone weighing NDSEG against GRFP: FAQ/Program states "the NDSEG Fellowship Program is non-deferrable" — so you cannot take GRFP first and defer NDSEG; the choose-one is immediate and irreversible.

The reapplication rule is confirmed verbatim and is genuinely unrestricted, but the binding constraint is TWO simultaneous clocks on the Eligibility page, not one: (a) "If enrolled, you must be or near the beginning (within first 2 years) of your Graduate study" AND (b) "Have at *least* THREE remaining years in your graduate degree program at the time of application." Criterion (b) is the one that actually closes the window first for many PhD students and is absent from the claim.

refuted.why: REFUTED as a derivation rule. The claim elevates "Fourth Tuesday in September, Annually Thereafter" to "the durable fact" and tells the reader to treat any single year's date as a mere snapshot. But the rule does not generate NSF's own posted date for the very cycle in question: in September 2026 the Tuesdays are 1, 8, 15, 22, 29 — the FOURTH Tuesday is 22 September 2026, while NSF posts 29 September 2026 (the fifth and last Tuesday) in the solicitation header, on the programme page, and in the June 2026 office-hour slides. A user who trusts the pattern over the posted date lands a week early in 2026 and has no way to know the rule is unreliable. (2027 does not expose the bug: 28 September 2027 is both the fourth and the last Tuesday.) The only rule that reproduces both posted dates is "last Tuesday in September" — which is not what NSF says. So the pattern sentence is NSF's own boilerplate, not a trustworthy generator; the enumerated posted date is the authoritative object and the pattern is only a coarse "late September, once a year" expectation.

refuted.why: Two problems, one narrow and one material. (1) The absolute "There is no NIH-interaction exclusion anywhere in this RFA" is too strong. refuted.why: The claim asserts "No prior-award disqualifier is published at all" and that TRDRP "does not key eligibility to prior funding history at all." That overstates. The 2027 Core Call publishes TWO restrictions that turn on other funding: (1) in the Postdoctoral Award Requirements section, verbatim: "The application must describe an original research project and not replicate the aims of any existing grants or applications held by the research advisor or mentors, whether funded by TRDRP or another source." This is an aims-overlap bar keyed to the MENTOR's funded and pending portfolio, and it can sink an otherwise eligible postdoc whose project sits inside their advisor's existing R01. (2) Under Pre-Funding Requirements, item 4, verbatim: "Resolution of any scientific overlap issues with other grants or pending applications." That is a condition of release of funds. The claim's underlying point (no NIH-style bar on holding or having held a federal career-development award or fellowship) survives, but stated as "no prior-award disqualifier at all" it is wrong in a direction that could mislead an applicant into ignoring mentor-grant overlap. The attributed verbatim "These templates will be made available for Letters of Intent that are invited to submit a Full Application" could not be found on any TRDRP page or PDF checked: the 2027 Core Call PDF (full text extracted, 46pp), the Postdoctoral Award mechanism page, what-we-fund, the Call-for-Applications FAQ, trainee-corner/apply-and-manage, the 2027 Core applicant webinar slides, and the 2027 SmartSimple applicant webinar slides. The Call's actual template language is different and says nothing about invitation-gating: "the current application templates for grant documentation must be used. See SmartSimple to download the latest templates. Applications failing to use the correct templates will be administratively rejected." The SUBSTANCE (Oct 29 is open only to invited LOIs) is independently supported by the Call's LOI process section, so the gate itself stands; it is the quotation that is unsupported and should not be presented as the funder's words.

corrections.corrected_value: No NIH-style bar on prior or concurrent funding history. BUT two published restrictions do turn on other funding and must be stated: (1) aims-overlap with the mentor's portfolio — "The application must describe an original research project and not replicate the aims of any existing grants or applications held by the research advisor or mentors, whether funded by TRDRP or another source" (2027 Core Call, Postdoctoral Award Requirements, p.19); (2) a pre-funding condition — "Resolution of any scientific overlap issues with other grants or pending applications" (2027 Core Call, Pre-Funding Requirements item 4, p.34). CONFIRMED, and this is the field the brief flagged as highest-stakes, so stating it precisely: there is NO programme-level prior-funding exclusion in the FY24 NOFO. Holding or having held NIJ or other federal awards disqualifies nobody. The hard gates are career-stage gates — Fellows: "Possess an academic (or research) doctorate terminal degree in their respective field", "Not have been awarded tenure by December 31, 2023", "Be the proposal PI if the project has multiple investigators". NIJ actively recruits the unfunded: "In this funding category, first-time grant recipients are encouraged to apply." The single place funding history bites is the optional New Investigator/Early Career Opportunity special consideration, which requires the PI at time of submission to: "Hold a non-tenured assistant professor appointment at an accredited institution of higher education in the United States or an equivalent full-time staff scientist position at a research institution in the United States"; "Have completed a terminal degree or post-graduate clinical training within the six (6) years prior to September 30, 2024"; and "Have never previously received NIJ funding as a PI on a research project with the exception of Graduate Research Fellows." Losing that bonus is not losing eligibility. Separately — and this is an organisational risk screen, not an applicant-eligibility rule — OJP checks SAM.gov exclusion status, and for anticipated awards over $250,000 "must review and consider any information about the applicant that appears in the non-public segment of the integrity and performance system accessible through SAM.gov."

refuted.why: 'One executive summary and one full proposal per PI per RA' is not in the RA. I searched DARPARA2502 Amendment 5 for any per-PI submission cap and found none. What the RA actually constrains is the topic area, not the count: 'Each submission (executive summary or full proposal) must specify ONE and only one TA for the submission and identify this TA on the submission's cover sheet.' Presenting a per-PI limit as a rule could wrongly deter a PI whose idea spans two TAs.

'Nothing to disclose beyond a single cover-sheet checkbox' is wrong. The mandatory Volume 1 (Technical & Management) cover sheet requires a full prior-DARPA disclosure table: 'List all past DARPA awards / DARPA Office: / Solicitation #: / Proposal Title: / Amount Awarded: / Performance Dates:' — in addition to 'Have you proposed to YFA before? [Yes or No] If yes what year'. An applicant told there is only a checkbox will arrive at the template unprepared.

Item 3 (former DARPA PMs) is truncated mid-word in the claim ('not eligibl') and the surrounding framing implies the same Senior-Personnel carve-out as items 1 and 2. It does not exist. The RA: 'Former DARPA PMs are not eligible to serve under this program in any capacity.' No carve-out at all.

The gloss 'a career-to-date total, not an annual rate, and it counts subaward money' is right on the last point but omits the RA's own arithmetic rule, footnote 13: 'To determine eligibility based on funding limitations, those who have served as co-PIs should include the share of the funds allocated to their contractual activity under those awards. If all PIs on an award are listed as "co-PIs" then an equal distribution to all such identified individuals should be used.' Counting whole award values rather than one's share would tell eligible people they are over the cap.

Presented as 'BOTH HALVES' of Section IV, but Section IV carries three further hard disqualifiers the claim never reaches: researchers at FFRDCs, UARCs, National Laboratories or other Government entities are 'not eligible to serve under this program in any capacity'; citizens of China, Cuba, Russia, Iran, Venezuela and North Korea are barred as Key or Senior Personnel unless one of three carve-outs is met; and the PI must be tenure-track, tenured within 3 years of the tenure date, or equivalent at a non-profit, and within 12 years of the doctorate. For an ECR audience the 12-year window and the national-lab bar are more likely to decide eligibility than the money cap.

'So mid-December feedback ... leaving roughly five weeks to write the full proposal' is a derived date that the source does not support. 15 October 2025 plus the RA's own 'approximately 45 calendar days' is ~29 November 2025, roughly 7.5 weeks before the 20 January 2026 deadline, not five. The 97-day figure quoted alongside it is correct.

'All 19 YFA cycles on grants.gov' — there are 18. A full grants.gov sweep of every DARPA office code returns exactly 18 YFA research announcements (13 DSO, 4 MTO, 1 BTO), and the claim's own list contains 18 entries, so the count contradicts itself. DARPARA2402, which appears in one USAspending award description as a YFA number, is in fact the 'Somnus' announcement — a USAspending data-entry artefact, not a 19th cycle.

corrections.corrected_value: Full Section IV / Overview eligibility set, quoted from DARPARA2502 Amendment 5. WHO MAY BE PI: 'The proposed Principal Investigator (PI) must be in a current tenured track faculty position, tenured faculty within 3 years of their tenure date, or an equivalent at a non-profit research institution within 12 years of the receipt of their doctorate.' WHAT DISQUALIFIES YOU AS PI: (1) 'Individuals who have received funding greater than $500,000 from DARPA or $1,250,000 from all DoD sources combined as either a Prime or subawardee PI or co-PI are not eligible to be Key Personnel (i.e., PI) under the YFA program, but may serve as Senior Personnel' — with footnote 13: co-PIs count only 'the share of the funds allocated to their contractual activity', equal split where everyone is listed as co-PI. (2) 'Individuals who have previously received a YFA Award as a PI are not eligible to be a PI for this or any future YFA program, but may serve as Senior Personnel.' DISQUALIFIES YOU ENTIRELY, no Senior Personnel fallback: (3) 'Former DARPA PMs are not eligible to serve under this program in any capacity.' (4) 'Researchers working at Federally Funded Research and Development Centers, University Affiliated Research Centers, National Laboratories, or other Government entities are not eligible to serve under this program in any capacity.' (5) 'Proposed Key or Senior Personnel who are citizens of China, Cuba, Russia, Iran, Venezuela, and North Korea are not eligible for inclusion on a YFA proposal unless one of the following conditions is met' — dual US citizenship, US Permanent Resident/Green Card, or in the application process for permanent residency. (6) All Key and Senior Personnel and all team members must be employed at a U.S. institution. Senior Personnel are subject to the citizenship requirements but 'not subject to tenure requirements or funding limitations'.

Section D repeats it: 'All applications must be received by 5:00 PM Eastern time on 30 October 2026.' Both gate dates verbatim in the Anticipated Schedule of Events table: 'Questions Regarding Eligibility and Technical Requirements ** 10/16/2026 5:00 pm' and 'Questions for Grants Officer Regarding Proposal Submission** 10/29/2026 5:00 pm', column headed 'Time (Local Eastern Time)'. INDEPENDENT FUNDER-PAGE CONFIRMATION the other agent could not obtain: ONR's own announcements page at onr.navy.mil renders for me and lists 'Fiscal Year (FY) 2027 Young Investigator Program (YIP) N0001426SF004 — Posted: August 17, 2026 4:29 PM EST — Full Proposals Due: October 30, 2026 5:00 PM EST', with the white-paper field blank. So the date does not depend on simpler.grants.gov at all. TWO PRECISION FIXES. (1) ONR's listing page says 'EST'; the NOFO says 'Eastern Time' / 'Local Eastern Time'. 30 October 2026 falls before DST ends (1 Nov 2026), so the operative zone is EDT, i.e. 21:00 UTC. refuted.why: The sub-claim that "the eligibility window slides one year per cycle" is contradicted by the two data points actually cited. The 2023 AFOSR flyer (FA9550-23-S-0001 era) states eligibility as Ph.D. "within the last seven years (no earlier than 01 April 2017)"; the FY2027 NOFO states "Doctorate no earlier than 01 April 2019". That is a 2-year slide across roughly 3 cycles, not one year per cycle, and the window also widened (7 years back from the flyer-era start vs. ~8 years back from the 01 May 2027 start). The related sub-claim "roughly 7.5 years before the anticipated 1 May start" is also wrong arithmetic: 01 April 2019 to 01 May 2027 is 8.1 years. The rest of deadline_pattern (annual, one competition per FY; FY2027 cadence Sept NOFO / Oct white paper / Dec proposal / 1 May award; prior cadence March-April FOA with June-July proposals; "The AFOSR open BAA updates annually in the March/April time frame") is confirmed verbatim.

Two errors inside an otherwise-confirmed field. (1) "about 8 months end-to-end from the white paper" is wrong: 09 October 2026 to 01 May 2027 is 6.7 months, call it 7. (2) "peer review by external subject-matter experts" over-specifies. The NOFO's F.2.a.2 says only "The peer review will use appropriate subject matter expert reviewers" -- it does not say external -- and the Overview says the opposite: "We will evaluate proposals using an internal review panel." The word external appears in the NOFO only in an unrelated GenAI restriction ("external reviewers are prohibited from using GenAI tools in the review"), so the composition of the peer-review panel is genuinely ambiguous in the source and should not be stated as external. Everything else in the field is confirmed verbatim, including both award-date quotes, the 06 November 2026 interim gate, the 20 April 2027 style selection notice date ("no later than 26 April 2027"), the budget-form requirement ("You must identify a date no later than 01 May 2027 as the anticipated start date in your proposal and budget"), and the go/no-go Programmatic Requirements Review citing EO 14303, EO 14332 and EO 14030, with "it will be removed from consideration" for failures.

corrections.corrected_value: Annual, one competition per federal fiscal year. FY2027 cadence: NOFO posted 8 Sep 2026, white paper due 9 Oct 2026, white-paper determination by 6 Nov 2026, invited full proposal due 4 Dec 2026, selection notice no later than 26 Apr 2027, awards by 1 May 2027. The cadence is NOT stable across cycles -- the 2023-era flyer shows "FOA posts: March/April on Grants.gov" with "Proposals Due: June/July" and no white-paper stage at all -- so re-check Grants.gov each year rather than assuming. The eligibility cut-off does move between cycles but NOT at a reliable one-year-per-cycle rate: 01 April 2017 in the 2023-era flyer (framed there as Ph.D. "within the last seven years") vs. 01 April 2019 for FY2027 -- a 2-year move across about 3 cycles, and ~8.1 years back from the 1 May 2027 start rather than 7.5. Treat the cut-off as a per-cycle lookup, not a formula. Separately confirmed: "The AFOSR open BAA updates annually in the March/April time frame."

corrections.corrected_value: About 5 months from full proposal to award (4 Dec 2026 to 1 May 2027) and about 7 months end-to-end from the white-paper deadline (9 Oct 2026 to 1 May 2027). Two-stage merit review: "Proposals will be subjected to programmatic and peer reviews." Programmatic review "will use AFOSR Program Officers and subject matter experts"; peer review "will use appropriate subject matter expert reviewers" -- the NOFO does not state these are external, and the Overview separately says "We will evaluate proposals using an internal review panel", so do not characterise the panel as external. Interim gate: white-paper determination "before COB on 06 November 2026". FY2027 adds a go/no-go Programmatic Requirements Review (initial screening) against EO 14303 "Gold Standard Science", EO 14332 and EO 14030 before the Full Evaluation; a proposal that fails "will be removed from consideration". Quotes confirmed: "We anticipate that we will notify proposers of selection or non-selection for award no later than 26 April 2027. We anticipate awards to be made by 01 May 2027, barring delays." and "You must identify a date no later than 01 May 2027 as the anticipated start date in your proposal and budget".

CONFIRMED AS WRITTEN and worth stating plainly: the FY2027 NOFO contains no prior-funding exclusion and no dollar cap on existing support. Section C.1 eligibility is only (i) "Doctorate no earlier than 01 April 2019"; U.S. citizen, national or permanent resident at time of proposal submission; full-time non-contractor permanent, career-competitive or tenure-track position (or a letter stating you will be considered for one if on a short-term appointment); and not at an FFRDC or DoW Laboratory. Holding an NSF CAREER, NIH or other DoD award does not disqualify you. Existing awards are handled purely as disclosure and overlap: Current and Pending (Other) Support "is used by AFOSR to assess: The capacity of the individual to carry out the proposed research. Any potential scientific and budgetary overlap or duplication across projects. The potential the individual is overcommitting themselves with the proposed project." AFOSR accepts the NSF common form. ADDITION the original claim omits, and it is a real eligibility trap in the same neighbourhood: "No domestic or foreign collaborators, funded or non-funded, are allowed for this single investigator award", and "There may not be co-PIs" except where the PI transfers institutions after the closing date and the primary institution adds the receiving institution as a sub-award. Also: annual budget must not exceed $150,000 and total $450,000 over three years -- "Proposals exceeding the annual $150,000 limit, the overall $450,000 threshold, or the three-year duration may be rejected without review."

corrections.corrected_value: CONFIRMED verbatim, with one caveat the original claim does not flag: the NOFO gives TWO non-identical exclusion lists and the safer reading is the narrower one. D.2.d.v: "Page Limitation - No more than twenty (20) single-sided pages. The cover page, table of contents, list of references, letters of support, curriculum vitae and list of ongoing and pending research support are excluded from the page limitations. The pages of proposals exceeding the page limit may not be included in the evaluation." But D.2.e says: "This page count does not include the following sections: Project Summary/Abstract, Curriculum Vitae, and the Bibliography & References" -- which omits letters of support, table of contents and current/pending support. Format otherwise: 8.5x11 paper, 1-inch margins, 1.5-line spacing, Times New Roman or Garamond 12pt, PDF attachments. Submission: Grants.gov only -- "We will not accept or evaluate any proposal submitted by any means other than through Grants.gov" -- using the SF 424 (R&R) Form Family, OMB 4040-0001, where "The SF 424 (R&R) Application for Federal assistance form must be your cover page. No pages may precede the SF 424 (R&R)", marked with the announcement number. A data management plan modelled on NSF's requirement is also required.

CONFIRMED, including the honesty about its thinness. The NOFO carries no sample application, annotated example or white-paper library. The funded-abstract mandate is real and quotable: "If you receive an award, we must publish your abstract to a searchable website available to the general public in accordance with Public Law 113-235. The website address is https://discover.dtic.mil/submit-documents/". The NOFO also spells out exactly what a white paper must contain, which is the closest thing to a template AFOSR offers: cover page with NOFO number, research topic title, and PI contact details; identification of proposed research and issues; potential impact on DAF and DoW capabilities; potential team members and development plans; proposed technical approaches (hypothesis, theories, concepts, approaches, data measurements, analysis); and "All publications and presentations must be identified". White papers are scored on just two equally weighted criteria: "(1) Technical merits of the proposed research and development. (2) Potential relationship of the proposed research and development to DoW missions." Practical route to examples: talk to the named Program Officer for your portfolio in the open BAA before writing -- "Proposers are encouraged to confer with the designated AFOSR Program Officer(s) prior to submitting a full proposal."
